1: # CLAUDE.md
2: 
3: Guidance for Claude Code when working on **Tuna TUI** v0.4.0 — a lean terminal music
4: player in Rust (ratatui TUI, yt-dlp → ffmpeg → rodio streaming, MIT). The
5: Spotify→YouTube port is **landed** (phases 1–4 of the original plan; see

8: ## What's here
9: 
10: - **UI layer — keep untouched**: `src/ui/*`, `src/app/*` (except `persist.rs`),
11:   `src/input/*`, `src/cover.rs`, `src/theme.rs`, `src/color.rs`, `src/gradient.rs`,
12:   `src/anim.rs`, `src/reactive.rs`. The UI is service-agnostic;
13:   it feeds on `LibItem`/`Section`/`ActionMenu` shapes and engine events only.
14: - **The service surface (what the port produced)**:
15:   - `src/yt/` (lib) — everything that talks to the `yt-dlp` CLI: `search` /
16:     `resolve` / `video_meta` / `playlist_entries`, untyped `-J` JSON-path reads.
17:     Offline-tested on canned `-J` dumps; live tests `#[ignore]`d.
18:   - `src/engine/` (lib) — `Expander` trait (`YtExpander` is the only impl;
19:     `examples/probe` drives it) → worker thread runs `ffmpeg -f s16le -ac 2
20:     -ar 44100 -` into rodio; watchdog re-resolves stalled streams.
21:     `src/audio/` holds the FFT `Visualizer` core (fed by `FfmpegSource`); the
22:     UI only renders the bands (`src/ui/visualizer.rs`).
23:     `Engine::queue()` mirrors the loaded list for the Queue view; `enqueue()`
24:     appends from the menu.
25:   - `src/browse.rs` (bin) — search / library sections / drill-ins, out of the

29:   - `src/actions.rs` (bin) — instant local menu (`build_action_menu`) and

31:   - `src/app/persist.rs` — `Store { liked/albums/artists/playlists/history }`

40: - **Key architecture facts** (verified 2026-08-16, port landed 2026-08-16):
41:   - **No typed serde structs** — everything is untyped JSON-path reads
42:     (`v["entries"][0]["title"]`); the yt-dlp `-J` consumer owns this pattern

85: ## Feature fidelity (post-port)
86: 
87: | Feature | Implementation | Fidelity |
88: |---|---|---|
89: | Search songs | `ytsearchN:` flat results (`spawn_search`) | keep |
90: | Search artists/albums/playlists | not in search (yt has no first-class entities); they live in the local library | approx |
91: | Home | local rolling history in `state.json` (play counts + recency) | local |
92: | Library (liked / albums / artists / playlists) | local `Store`; external playlists drill in via YouTube | approx |
93: | Playlist drill-in | `--flat-playlist`; local adds win over the network copy | keep-ish |
94: | Album drill-in | slug search (`yt:album:<slug>`) | approx |
95: | Track meta + cover | engine ships `EngineMeta` for every track | keep |
96: | Lyrics | lrclib (unchanged) | keep |
97: | Playback | `-g` → `ffmpeg` → PCM → rodio + same FFT visualizer | new engine |
98: | Seek / scrub | `-ss` restart on stream (~1s); local display counts delivered frames | approx |
99: | Volume / shuffle / repeat | local mixer + local queue ops | keep |
100: | Song radio | mix flat-extracted at one inner-page cap (`--playlist-end`), `RD<id>` → `RDAMVM<id>` → search-built pseudo-radio fallback chain | approx (good) |
101: | Queue / add-to-queue | engine-loaded list + `enqueue`; menu Queue appends | keep |
102: | Like / follow / save | local stores, menu entries keep shape | local |
103: | Copy link / open | `youtube.com/watch?v=<id>` etc (`uri_to_url`) | keep |
104: | Resume on startup | same `state.json` shape + seek | keep |
105: | Media keys / MPRIS (souvlaki), txc, visualizer | untouched | keep |
106: | Multi-device (Connect) | **no YouTube equivalent — inherently lost** | lost |
107: 
108: Standing risks (from the port, still true): YouTube ToS/throttling grey zone

113: restart on throttled streams. The radio timeout/fallback work (bead

147: ## Beads Issue Tracker
148: 
149: This project uses **bd (beads)** for issue tracking. Run `bd prime` to see full workflow context and commands.
150: 
151: ### Quick Reference
152: 
153: ```bash
154: bd ready              # Find available work
155: bd show <id>          # View issue details
156: bd update <id> --claim  # Claim work
157: bd close <id>         # Complete work
158: ```
159: 
160: ### Rules
161: 
162: - Use `bd` for ALL task tracking — do NOT use TodoWrite, TaskCreate, or markdown TODO lists
163: - Run `bd prime` for detailed command reference and session close protocol
164: - Use `bd remember` for persistent knowledge — do NOT use MEMORY.md files
165: 
166: **Enforcement (live 2026-08-20):** two hooks back this up. `.claude/hooks/bd-enforce.sh`
167: (local, PreToolUse) hard-blocks TodoWrite/TaskCreate, MEMORY.md / auto-memory writes,
168: and markdown TODO files — `bd create`/`bd remember` instead — and soft-warns on source
169: edits with zero in_progress beads; `install`/`status`/`selftest` modes. `scripts/bd-enforce.sh`
170: (committed, pre-commit) requires a bead ref (`Myx-...`) in commit messages unless the scope
171: is merge/revert/release/chore/docs/ci/build/refactor. Both are wired into this repo's hooks.
172: 
173: **Architecture in one line:** issues live in a local Dolt DB; sync uses `refs/dolt/data` on your git remote; `.beads/issues.jsonl` is a passive export. See https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/blob/main/docs/SYNC_CONCEPTS.md for details and anti-patterns.
174: 
175: ## Agent Context Profiles
176: 
177: The managed Beads block is task-tracking guidance, not permission to override repository, user, or orchestrator instructions.
178: 
179: - **Conservative (default)**: Use `bd` for task tracking. Do not run git commits, git pushes, or Dolt remote sync unless explicitly asked. At handoff, report changed files, validation, and suggested next commands.
180: - **Minimal**: Keep tool instruction files as pointers to `bd prime`; use the same conservative git policy unless active instructions say otherwise.
181: - **Team-maintainer**: Only when the repository explicitly opts in, agents may close beads, run quality gates, commit, and push as part of session close. A current "do not commit" or "do not push" instruction still wins.
182: 
183: ## Session Completion
184: 
185: This protocol applies when ending a Beads implementation workflow. It is subordinate to explicit user, repository, and orchestrator instructions.
186: 
187: 1. **File issues for remaining work** - Create beads for anything that needs follow-up
188: 2. **Run quality gates** (if code changed) - Tests, linters, builds
189: 3. **Update issue status** - Close finished work, update in-progress items
190: 4. **Handle git/sync by active profile**:
191:    ```bash
192:    # Conservative/minimal/default: report status and proposed commands; wait for approval.
193:    git status
194: 
195:    # Team-maintainer opt-in only, unless current instructions forbid it:
196:    git pull --rebase
197:    bd dolt push
198:    git push
199:    git status
200:    ```
201: 5. **Hand off** - Summarize changes, validation, issue status, and any blocked sync/commit/push step
202: 
203: **Critical rules:**
204: - Explicit user or orchestrator instructions override this Beads block.
205: - Do not commit or push without clear authority from the active profile or the current user request.
206: - If a required sync or push is blocked, stop and report the exact command and error.

1: //! The YouTube layer — everything that talks to the `yt-dlp` CLI.
2: //!
3: //! One-way dependency, like `api/`: spawns the yt-dlp process and hands plain
4: //! data back to the app over its return values; nothing here touches `App` or
5: //! the render tree.
6: //!
7: //! Phase 1 of the Spotify → YouTube port. Read-only and self-contained; every
8: //! parser is tested offline on canned `-J` JSON, so developing against it needs
9: //! no YouTube account, no cookies and no network. The live smoke tests that do
10: //! need a network are marked `#[ignore]`, matching the project convention.
11: 
12: //! The phase-2 engine and phase-3 api layer are the callers; fields stay public
13: //! so the bin-side expander can repackage rows. The allow drops those few items
14: //! no caller has reached yet.
15: #![allow(dead_code)]

17: use crate::config;
18: use crate::liblog::liblog;
19: use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};

24: /// A cap on concurrent yt-dlp children (F17): every app surface (engine
25: /// per-track resolve, search thread, drill-in thread, radio chains) funnels a
26: /// fresh `Command` through `yt_stdout`, and each child is a new ~50–80MB
27: /// Python with a ~300–500ms startup. Two permits let two surfaces overlap
28: /// without stacking a herd. Contention beyond the budget FAILS OPEN (see
29: /// [`wait_for_permit`]) — never a spurious failure, which the engine would
30: /// read as a dropped stream and burn a recovery retry on.
31: ///
32: /// `tokio::sync::Semaphore` rather than `std`: no `std::sync::Semaphore`
33: /// exists on the toolchain this crate builds with (rustc 1.97.1); tokio's is
34: /// already a dependency of the `streaming` feature that gates this module.
35: static YTDLP_PERMIT: Semaphore = Semaphore::const_new(2);
36: 
37: /// How long a single yt-dlp socket can stall before the process gives up. A
38: /// hung network must never wedge a worker thread forever; the app's own
39: /// radio/playback deadlines sit above this (see `RADIO_TIMEOUT_SECS`).
40: const SOCKET_TIMEOUT_SECS: u32 = 10;
41: /// Extra headroom added to [`SOCKET_TIMEOUT_SECS`] when sizing the process
42: /// deadline: yt-dlp's own retry/internal handling can outlive one socket
43: /// timeout by a few seconds, and a stalled worker must still give up.
44: const DEADLINE_MARGIN_SECS: u32 = 5;
45: 
46: /// One playable YouTube video: a search result, a playlist entry, or a resolved
47: /// single video. Rows that cannot be played (no video id) are dropped by the
48: /// parsers rather than surfaced as empty rows.
49: pub struct YtVideo {
50:     /// Canonical internal uri: `yt:video:<id>` — the id itself is derivable
51:     /// (`track_id_from_uri`), so rows carry only the uri.
52:     pub uri: String,
53:     pub title: String,
54:     /// Best-known performer name: `artist` when MusicBrainz-tagged, else the
55:     /// channel/uploader name. Empty on flat playlist rows, which are title-only.
56:     pub artist: String,
57:     /// Absent on all but a few MusicBrainz-tagged videos.
58:     pub album: Option<String>,
59:     /// Missing on some flat playlist rows; `None` rows can't drive the progress
60:     /// bar or the lrclib duration key until enriched.
61:     pub duration_ms: Option<u32>,
62:     /// Best available thumbnail (last, largest in the array), when present.
63:     pub thumbnail: Option<String>,
64: }
65: 
66: /// A playable stream: the direct audio URL plus the metadata playback needs.
67: pub struct StreamInfo {
68:     pub url: String,
69:     pub video: YtVideo,
70: }
71: 
72: /// `ytsearchN:` — N YouTube video results for a query. Fast (one request):
73: /// flat mode uses only the search API's own metadata, no per-video resolution.
74: pub fn search(query: &str, limit: usize) -> Vec<YtVideo> {
75:     let limit = limit.max(1);
76:     let Some(root) = yt_json(
77:         &["--flat-playlist", &format!("ytsearch{limit}:{query}")],
78:         None,
79:     ) else {
80:         return Vec::new();
81:     };
82:     entries(&root)
83: }
84: 
85: /// Full metadata for one video, from a bare video id, a `yt:video:` uri, or a
86: /// `youtube.com/watch?v=` URL. `--no-playlist` keeps a video that happens to be
87: /// inside a mix from expanding into its whole playlist.
88: pub fn video_meta(url_or_id: &str) -> Option<YtVideo> {
89:     let url = crate::util::video_url(url_or_id)?;
90:     let root = yt_json(&["--no-playlist", &url], None)?;
91:     video_from(&root)
92: }
93: 
94: /// The direct audio stream URL for one video, plus the metadata resolution
95: /// needed to play it (title, duration, thumbnail, artist) — one `-J` call
96: /// carries both (the `-f`/extractor-args policy below, then [`pick_url`]).
97: pub fn resolve(url_or_id: &str) -> Option<StreamInfo> {
98:     let url = crate::util::video_url(url_or_id)?;
99:     let configured = config::get().audio_format.clone();
100:     // `bestaudio/best` under the android client means `best` (the muxed
101:     // stream) — but a user who set `bestaudio` without a fallback must not
102:     // hard-fail resolution, so always carry the `/best` tail.
103:     let format = if configured.contains('/') {
104:         configured.clone()
105:     } else {
106:         format!("{configured}/best")
107:     };
108:     let root = yt_json(
109:         &[
110:             "--no-playlist",
111:             "-f",
112:             &format,
113:             &url,
114:             "--extractor-args",
115:             &format!("youtube:player_client={STREAM_PLAYER_CLIENT}"),
116:         ],
117:         None,
118:     )?;
119:     let video = video_from(&root)?;
120:     let stream = pick_url(&root, &configured)?;
121:     Some(StreamInfo {
122:         url: stream.to_string(),
123:         video,
124:     })
125: }
126: 
127: /// How long a radio request may take before the app gives up. The station
128: /// fetch is capped to one inner-page (~4s), so this only covers the rare
129: /// fallback chain (mix-id variants + a search-built station) and genuine
130: /// network stalls — 12s was shorter than an un-capped mix's pagination alone
131: /// (20s+), which made healthy-but-large mixes read as endpoint timeouts.
132: pub const RADIO_TIMEOUT_SECS: u64 = 20;
133: 
134: /// How many entries the radio fetch asks for — the engine's station cap,
135: /// clipped to one or two inner-pages at most: un-capped, yt-dlp paginates the
136: /// whole mix — hundreds of rows across 15+ sequential API pages, 20s+ even on
137: /// a healthy network (measured 2026-08-16) — and the app's radio deadline
138: /// fires for what is really a too-greedy fetch. `--playlist-end` at this cap
139: /// costs ~4s per mix. The clip below is `min(station cap, 40)` — it can never
140: /// paginate past the engine's station slice, so no pin is needed.
141: const RADIO_FETCH_LIMIT: usize = if crate::engine::RADIO_LIMIT < 40 {
142:     crate::engine::RADIO_LIMIT
143: } else {
144:     40
145: };
146: 
147: /// Candidate mix URLs for a seed video, in preference order: the canonical
148: /// `RD<id>` mix, then its autoplay-video variant `RDAMVM<id>`. The id cannot

150: /// watch HTML carry the current video's mix id (verified 2026-08-16); the
151: /// convention is deterministic (`RD` + video id, confirmed by the page's own
152: /// `start_radio` command URLs), so these are the only two shapes worth trying.
153: fn radio_candidates(id: &str) -> Vec<String> {
154:     vec![
155:         format!("https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={id}&list=RD{id}"),
156:         format!("https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={id}&list=RDAMVM{id}"),
157:     ]
158: }

160: /// A radio station for a seed video id: the first mix candidate that serves
161: /// rows, else a search-built pseudo-radio. YouTube has no mix for fresh or
162: /// obscure uploads — `--flat-playlist` on their `RD<id>` URL degrades to a
163: /// single-video dump (zero entries), which used to read as a hard radio
164: /// failure. The pseudo-radio resolves the seed for its title, searches that
165: /// flat, and drops the seed itself from the results.
166: pub fn radio_entries(id: &str, cancel: Arc<AtomicBool>) -> Vec<YtVideo> {
167:     let limit = RADIO_FETCH_LIMIT.to_string();
168:     for url in radio_candidates(id) {

171:         // request's signature; the caller (spawn_radio's timeout) has already

173:         if cancel.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
174:             return Vec::new();
175:         }
176:         if let Some(root) = yt_json(

178:             Some(cancel.clone()),

180:             let rows = entries(&root);
181:             if !rows.is_empty() {
182:                 return rows;
183:             }
184:             liblog(format!("yt: {url} served no playlist rows"));
185:         }

200: /// the station is a flat search on that title.
201: fn pseudo_radio(id: &str, cancel: Arc<AtomicBool>) -> Vec<YtVideo> {
202:     let Some(seed) = yt_json(
203:         &["--flat-playlist", &format!("ytsearch1:{id}")],
204:         Some(cancel.clone()),

207:         return Vec::new();
208:     };
209:     // F13: check between the two legs — the search-backed station is two

211:     if cancel.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
212:         return Vec::new();

214:     let query = pseudo_radio_query(&seed.title, &seed.artist);
215:     if query.is_empty() {
216:         return Vec::new();

218:     let Some(root) = yt_json(
219:         &[
220:             "--flat-playlist",
221:             &format!("ytsearch{}:{query}", RADIO_FETCH_LIMIT),
222:         ],
223:         Some(cancel),
224:     ) else {
225:         return Vec::new();
226:     };

228:         .into_iter()
229:         .filter(|v| v.uri != format!("yt:video:{id}"))
230:         .collect()

236: fn pseudo_radio_query(title: &str, artist: &str) -> String {

291:     // rather than vanishing silently (the caller can't tell the difference).
292:     if root["entries"].is_null() {
293:         liblog(format!("yt: {url} is not a playlist dump; no entries"));
294:         return Vec::new();
295:     }
296:     entries(&root)
297: }
298: 
299: /// The contents of a context kind. One table owns the kind → resource
300: /// mapping every layer consumes: playback expansion and the drill-in view
301: /// used to re-implement it separately and drifted on the channel URL shape.
302: /// `video` is absent on purpose — a single track's contents are itself, and
303: /// both callers already pass it through.
304: pub fn resolve_kind(kind: &str, id: &str, limit: usize) -> Vec<YtVideo> {
305:     match kind {
306:         "playlist" => playlist_entries(&crate::util::playlist_uri(id)),
307:         "channel" => playlist_entries(&crate::util::channel_videos_url(id)),
308:         "album" => search(id, limit),
309:         _ => Vec::new(),
310:     }
311: }
312: 
313: /// `Videos` rows from any playlist-shaped `-J` dump (`entries:` array).
314: fn entries(root: &serde_json::Value) -> Vec<YtVideo> {
315:     root["entries"]
316:         .as_array()
317:         .into_iter()
318:         .flatten()
319:         .filter_map(video_from)
320:         .collect()
321: }
322: 
323: /// One `entries[]` row -> `YtVideo`. `None` drops rows with no video id — the
324: /// flat-playlist equivalent of `api/library.rs`'s region-locked-row skip.
325: fn video_from(v: &serde_json::Value) -> Option<YtVideo> {
326:     let id = v["id"].as_str()?;
327:     let title = v["title"].as_str().unwrap_or("").to_string();
328:     let artist = v["artist"]
329:         .as_str()
330:         .or_else(|| v["channel"].as_str())
331:         .or_else(|| v["uploader"].as_str())
332:         .unwrap_or("")
333:         .to_string();
334:     let album = v["album"].as_str().map(String::from);
335:     let duration_ms = v["duration"]
336:         .as_u64()
337:         // checked_mul: `s * 1000` would wrap/panic on a hostile `-J` dump
338:         // (u64::MAX × 1000 overflows before the u32 try_from can guard it).
339:         .and_then(|s| s.checked_mul(1000))
340:         .and_then(|ms| u32::try_from(ms).ok());
341:     let thumbnail = largest_thumbnail(v);
342:     let uri = format!("yt:video:{id}");
343:     Some(YtVideo {
344:         uri,
345:         title,
346:         artist,
347:         album,
348:         duration_ms,
349:         thumbnail,
350:     })
351: }
352: 
353: /// The last thumbnail in the array — yt-dlp orders `thumbnails` small→large, so
354: /// the last is the biggest actual frame. Falls back to the bare `thumbnail`.
355: fn largest_thumbnail(v: &serde_json::Value) -> Option<String> {
356:     v["thumbnails"]
357:         .as_array()
358:         .and_then(|a| a.last())
359:         .and_then(|t| t["url"].as_str())
360:         .or_else(|| v["thumbnail"].as_str())
361:         .map(String::from)
362: }
363: 
364: /// Wait up to `deadline` for one of `p`'s permits, polling every 50ms.
365: /// `None` means the budget is exhausted: the caller MUST fail open (spawn
366: /// anyway and block for a permit) — a permit-shaped `None` must never surface
367: /// as a request failure, because `yt_stdout`'s `None` is a dropped stream to
368: /// the engine. In production `None` only appears under pathological
369: /// contention, where the fail-open fallback blocks until a permit frees
370: /// (unbounded wait; the single-permit cap is retained).
371: fn wait_for_permit(p: &Semaphore, deadline: Instant) -> Option<SemaphorePermit<'_>> {
372:     loop {
373:         if let Ok(permit) = p.try_acquire() {
374:             return Some(permit);
375:         }
376:         if Instant::now() >= deadline {
377:             return None;
378:         }
379:         std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50));
380:     }
381: }
382: 
383: /// Run `yt-dlp … -J` and parse its dumped JSON.
384: fn yt_json(extra: &[&str], cancel: Option<Arc<AtomicBool>>) -> Option<serde_json::Value> {
385:     yt_stdout(&["-J"], extra, cancel).and_then(|s| serde_json::from_str(&s).ok())
386: }
387: 
388: /// The stream leg is resolved with the `android` player client. On this box
389: /// (verified 2026-08-16, bead Myx-jqp) URLs from the default/web/tv clients
390: /// stall at the transport level — ffmpeg connects and receives 0 bytes in
391: /// 15 s, while the `android` client's URL flows instantly (~180 ms to first
392: /// PCM, 3/3 runs vs 0/9 for the others). A stalled URL starves the engine's
393: /// prebuffer → silent playback, ALSA underrun errors, frozen position and
394: /// visualizer, and watchdog rebuild loops.
395: ///
396: /// Trade-off: the android client exposes no audio-only itags — `-f bestaudio`
397: /// hard-fails under it, so the `/best` fallback below always lands on the
398: /// muxed (360p video + audio) stream, wasting bandwidth the engine never
399: /// decodes. That cost is deliberate: an unthrottled stream is worth 3× the
400: /// bytes; a user-set `audio_format` without a fallback is tolerated by
401: /// appending `/best` rather than letting resolution fail.
402: const STREAM_PLAYER_CLIENT: &str = "android";
403: 
404: /// Pull the direct stream URL out of a `-J` info dump — the same pick the old
405: /// `-g -f <configured>/best` leg made, now from the dump's own data:
406: /// 1. a `formats[]` entry whose `format_id` equals a bare `configured` (a
407: ///    user's `audio_format = "251"` must select that exact itag);
408: /// 2. otherwise the *last playable* entry — the android dump appends
409: ///    storyboard entries (`sb*`, both codecs "none") after the real stream,
410: ///    so the naive "last entry" would hand back a storyboard URL;
411: /// 3. finally the info dict's own top-level `url` — which with `-f` active is
412: ///    exactly the format `-g` would have printed.
413: fn pick_url<'a>(root: &'a serde_json::Value, configured: &str) -> Option<&'a str> {
414:     if let Some(entries) = root["formats"].as_array() {
415:         if !configured.contains('/') {
416:             if let Some(f) = entries
417:                 .iter()
418:                 .find(|f| f["format_id"].as_str() == Some(configured))
419:                 .and_then(|f| f["url"].as_str())
420:             {
421:                 return Some(f);
422:             }
423:         }
424:         if let Some(f) = entries.iter().rev().find(|f| {
425:             let playable = f["vcodec"].as_str().is_some_and(|v| v != "none")
426:                 || f["acodec"].as_str().is_some_and(|a| a != "none");
427:             playable && f["url"].as_str().is_some()
428:         }) {
429:             return f["url"].as_str();
430:         }
431:     }
432:     root["url"].as_str()
433: }
434: 
435: /// Run the configured yt-dlp binary with `base + extra` args and capture
436: /// stdout; `None` on launch failure, non-zero exit, or invalid UTF-8. Errors
437: /// are logged, not propagated — the api layer's Option/empty convention.
438: ///
439: /// Two bounds keep a yt-dlp child from ever wedging a worker thread:
440: /// `--retries 1` cuts yt-dlp's own default retry chain (which can sleep for
441: /// minutes on a 429), and the child is killed outright once it outlives
442: /// `SOCKET_TIMEOUT_SECS` + a small margin (a stalled socket must not hold a
443: /// blocking thread hostage while the app's own deadline has given up on it).
444: ///
445: /// The pipes MUST be drained while the child runs: a `-J` dump is ~600 KB and
446: /// yt-dlp blocks on a full 64 KB pipe unless something reads it, so a plain
447: /// poll-and-kill loop would deadlock until the deadline kills the child.
448: /// Reader threads therefore own the drains; the caller thread owns the child
449: /// (for `try_wait`/`kill`, which need `&mut`) and joins the readers once the
450: /// process is gone. Killing guarantees EOF on both pipes, so the joins always
451: /// return.
452: fn yt_stdout(base: &[&str], extra: &[&str], cancel: Option<Arc<AtomicBool>>) -> Option<String> {
453:     let bin = config::get().ytdlp_path.clone();
454:     yt_stdout_with_bin(&bin, base, extra, cancel)
455: }
456: 
457: /// The [`yt_stdout`] core with the binary injected — the config read stays at
458: /// the public boundary so tests can point the seam at a fake binary and run
459: /// the cancellability (F13) and concurrency-cap (F17) paths fully offline.
460: fn yt_stdout_with_bin(
461:     bin: &str,
462:     base: &[&str],
463:     extra: &[&str],
464:     cancel: Option<Arc<AtomicBool>>,
465: ) -> Option<String> {
466:     // F17: the RAII permit is held across the child's WHOLE life — spawn
467:     // through both drain joins — and drops on every early-return path below.
468:     // The bounded wait shares the child's own deadline; on budget exhaustion
469:     // the wait fails OPEN immediately (run unpermitted, log it) — an
470:     // unbounded blocking acquire here would hold the engine worker past its
471:     // resolve deadline, so the cap degrades to today's concurrency instead of
472:     // manufacturing a hang (audit F17 regression caution).
473:     let deadline =
474:         Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs((SOCKET_TIMEOUT_SECS + DEADLINE_MARGIN_SECS) as u64);
475:     let _permit = match wait_for_permit(&YTDLP_PERMIT, deadline) {
476:         Some(permit) => Some(permit),
477:         None => {
478:             liblog("yt: yt-dlp budget exhausted — running unpermitted (fail-open)");
479:             None
480:         }
481:     };
482:     let mut child = std::process::Command::new(bin)
483:         .args([
484:             "--no-warnings",
485:             "--socket-timeout",
486:             &SOCKET_TIMEOUT_SECS.to_string(),
487:             "--retries",
488:             "1",
489:         ])
490:         .args(base)
491:         // A TUI's stdin must never leak into the CLI child: with tuna-tui run under a
492:         // pipe (tests, streaming, probes) yt-dlp can stall on an inherited,
493:         // never-EOF stdin instead of doing its job. ffmpeg gets the same
494:         // treatment (`spawn_ffmpeg`).
495:         .stdin(std::process::Stdio::null())
496:         .args(extra)
497:         // Optional session cookies (`--cookies`): without them private
498:         // playlists / history are inaccessible and traffic is bot-checked.
499:         .args(match &config::get().cookies_file {
500:             Some(path) => vec!["--cookies", path.as_str()],
501:             None => vec![],
502:         })
503:         .stdout(std::process::Stdio::piped())
504:         .stderr(std::process::Stdio::piped())
505:         .spawn()
506:         .ok()?;
507:     let mut stdout = child.stdout.take();
508:     let mut stderr = child.stderr.take();
509:     let stdout_reader = std::thread::spawn(move || drain(&mut stdout));
510:     let stderr_reader = std::thread::spawn(move || drain(&mut stderr));
511:     let status = loop {
512:         match child.try_wait() {
513:             Ok(Some(status)) => break status,
514:             Ok(None) => {}
515:             Err(_) => return None,
516:         }
517:         // F13: a per-request cancel (spawn_radio's timeout Err branch sets it)
518:         // kills the child on the next 50ms poll instead of letting a radio
519:         // chain keep spawning Python for ~40s after the UI has given up.
520:         if cancel.as_ref().is_some_and(|c| c.load(Ordering::Relaxed)) {
521:             liblog(format!("yt: {bin} killed on cancellation"));
522:             let _ = child.kill();
523:             break child.wait().ok()?;
524:         }
525:         if Instant::now() >= deadline {
526:             liblog(format!("yt: {bin} killed after exceeding its deadline"));
527:             let _ = child.kill();
528:             break child.wait().ok()?;
529:         }
530:         std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50));
531:     };
532:     // Both pipes EOF once the process is gone (kill included), so these joins
533:     // cannot hang.
534:     let out = stdout_reader.join().ok()?;
535:     let err = stderr_reader.join().ok()?;
536:     if !status.success() {
537:         let code = status.code().unwrap_or(-1);
538:         let tail = String::from_utf8_lossy(&err)
539:             .lines()
540:             .next_back()
541:             .unwrap_or("")
542:             .to_string();
543:         liblog(format!(
544:             "yt: {bin} exited {code}: {tail} (args {:?})",
545:             extra.iter().take(3).collect::<Vec<_>>()
546:         ));
547:         return None;
548:     }
549:     String::from_utf8(out).ok()
550: }
551: 
552: /// Read one pipe to EOF into a vector. Runs on the reader threads; EOF is
553: /// guaranteed by the process exiting (or being killed).
554: fn drain<R: std::io::Read + Send>(pipe: &mut Option<R>) -> Vec<u8> {
555:     let mut buf = Vec::new();
556:     if let Some(pipe) = pipe.as_mut() {
557:         let _ = pipe.read_to_end(&mut buf);
558:     }
559:     buf
560: }

870:         std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(200));

356: /// The queue pair is the engine's "append" surface: the output side is appended
357: /// to the player once (it plays silence when empty), and each track is a
358: /// `append_with_signal`d sound on the input side whose exposed receiver is the
359: /// EOF signal. `Player` keeps its own queue private, so the pair sits outside
360: /// it — volume/pause/play still go through the `Player`.
361: fn open_output() -> Result<(
362:     MixerDeviceSink,
363:     Player,
364:     Arc<rodio::queue::SourcesQueueInput>,
365: )> {
366:     // Device faults (cpal's `BufferUnderrun` on an ALSA/PipeWire xrun) go to
367:     // the tuna-tui log instead of rodio's default raw `eprintln!` storming the
368:     // terminal beside the TUI. The closure captures nothing, so the builder
369:     // stays `Clone` for `open_sink_or_fallback`'s config fallback.
370:     let mut sink = DeviceSinkBuilder::from_default_device()
371:         .map_err(|e| anyhow!("audio device: {e}"))?
372:         .with_error_callback(|err| liblog(format!("audio stream error: {err}")))
373:         .open_sink_or_fallback()
374:         .context("open audio device")?;
375:     sink.log_on_drop(false);
376:     let player = Player::connect_new(sink.mixer());
377:     let (queue_in, queue_out) = rodio::queue::queue(true);
378:     player.append(queue_out);
379:     Ok((sink, player, queue_in))
380: }
381: 
382: /// Start the engine. Synchronous (it needs no runtime); the worker + watchdog
383: /// threads are spawned here. `expander` resolves uris into streams; `events`
384: /// receives the EngineEvent stream; `meta_tx` receives in-band metadata for
385: /// yt: tracks.
386: pub fn run(
387:     events: flume::Sender<EngineEvent>,
388:     meta_tx: flume::Sender<EngineMeta>,
389:     initial_volume_pct: u8,
390:     expander: Arc<dyn Expander>,
391: ) -> Result<Engine> {
392:     let bands = VisBands::shared();
393:     let (sink, player, queue) = open_output()?;
394:     let (cmds_tx, cmds_rx) = flume::unbounded::<Cmd>();
395:     let health = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Health {
396:         playing: false,
397:         last_progress: Instant::now(),
398:     }));
399: 
400:     let queue_snapshot = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
401:     let worker = Worker {
402:         sink,
403:         player,
404:         queue,
405:         bands: Arc::clone(&bands),
406:         events,
407:         meta_tx,
408:         cmds: cmds_rx,
409:         expander: Arc::clone(&expander),
410:         queue_snapshot: Arc::clone(&queue_snapshot),
411:         state: PlayerState {
412:             tracks: Vec::new(),
413:             cursor: 0,
414:             history: Vec::new(),
415:             shuffle: false,
416:             repeat: false,
417:             volume: initial_volume_pct.clamp(0, 100) as f32 / 100.0,
418:             playing: false,
419:         },
420:         current: None,
421:         health: Arc::clone(&health),
422:         drop_streak: 0,
423:         last_seen_frames: 0,
424:         last_correction: Instant::now(),
425:         // Cloning the once-built blocking client (Arc-fee) — constructed by
426:         // `httpcache::warm_blocking_client` before the runtime started.
427:         client: crate::httpcache::blocking_client().clone(),
428:         pending: None,
429:         recovery: None,
430:         paused: None,
431:     };
432:     std::thread::Builder::new()
433:         .name("tuna-engine".to_string())
434:         .spawn(move || worker.run())?;
435:     spawn_watchdog(Arc::clone(&health), cmds_tx.clone());
436: 
437:     Ok(Engine {
438:         bands,
439:         inner: Arc::new(Inner {
440:             cmds: cmds_tx,
441:             expander,
442:             queue: queue_snapshot,
443:         }),
444:     })
445: }
446: 
447: /// Poll for a stuck stream and ask the worker to rebuild it.
448: ///
449: /// Holds only a *weak* sender: when the app drops its last [`Engine`], the
450: /// worker's channel disconnects, the loop's `upgrade()` returns `None`, and
451: /// this thread leaves — letting the worker see `Disconnected` and run its
452: /// teardown instead of lingering anonymous forever (the strong sender held by
453: /// the watchdog used to make that teardown unreachable).
454: fn spawn_watchdog(health: Arc<Mutex<Health>>, cmds: flume::Sender<Cmd>) {
455:     let weak = cmds.downgrade();
456:     let _ = std::thread::Builder::new()
457:         .name("tuna-watchdog".to_string())
458:         .spawn(move || loop {
459:             std::thread::sleep(HEALTH_CHECK);
460:             // `upgrade()` is also the liveness probe: none left → retire.
461:             let Some(cmds) = weak.upgrade() else {
462:                 return;
463:             };
464:             let h = match health.lock() {
465:                 Ok(h) => h,
466:                 Err(p) => p.into_inner(),
467:             };
468:             if h.playing && h.last_progress.elapsed() > STALL_AFTER {
469:                 drop(h);
470:                 // The worker clears `playing` while it rebuilds, so this can
471:                 // never stack recoveries; it re-arms at the next poll.
472:                 let _ = cmds.send(Cmd::Recover);
473:             }
474:         });
475: }
476: 
477: struct Worker {
478:     /// Held alive for the worker's whole life: dropping it stops the device.
479:     #[allow(dead_code)] // the guard's whole job is to be held, never read
480:     sink: MixerDeviceSink,
481:     player: Player,
482:     /// The per-track sound queue: tracks are appended here, EOF signals come
483:     /// back from its receivers.
484:     queue: Arc<rodio::queue::SourcesQueueInput>,
485:     bands: Arc<Mutex<VisBands>>,
486:     events: flume::Sender<EngineEvent>,
487:     meta_tx: flume::Sender<EngineMeta>,
488:     cmds: flume::Receiver<Cmd>,
489:     expander: Arc<dyn Expander>,
490:     /// The public mirror of the loaded list (`Engine::queue`).
491:     queue_snapshot: Arc<Mutex<Vec<String>>>,
492:     state: PlayerState,
493:     current: Option<CurrentTrack>,
494:     health: Arc<Mutex<Health>>,
495:     /// Consecutive short-EOF drops on the current track (mirrors
496:     /// [`RECOVERY_ATTEMPTS`]); reset on a natural end or a new track.
497:     drop_streak: u32,
498:     /// The last frame count seen (stall detection needs deltas).
499:     last_seen_frames: u64,
500:     last_correction: Instant,
501:     client: reqwest::blocking::Client,
502:     /// A user command that pre-empted a recovery retry-sleep; handled before
503:     /// anything queued behind it.
504:     pending: Option<Cmd>,
505:     /// The track a recovery is rebuilding, while `current` is nowhere. The
506:     /// watchdog and a pre-empted resume use it to re-enter the rebuild loop
507:     /// instead of losing the track.
508:     recovery: Option<(String, u32)>,
509:     /// The paused track's stream, while `current` is nowhere: the URL stays
510:     /// cached so a resume can restart without re-resolving. Cleared on every
511:     /// transition out of the pause state (next/prev/stop/load/teardown) so it
512:     /// can never resurrect a stale stream on a later resume.
513:     paused: Option<PausedTrack>,
514: }
515: 
516: impl Worker {
517:     fn run(mut self) {
518:         self.player.set_volume(self.state.volume);
519:         loop {
520:             match self.cmds.recv_timeout(TICK) {
521:                 Ok(cmd) => self.handle(cmd),
522:                 Err(flume::RecvTimeoutError::Timeout) => self.tick(),
523:                 Err(flume::RecvTimeoutError::Disconnected) => break,
524:             }
525:             if let Some(pre) = self.pending.take() {
526:                 self.handle(pre);
527:                 // The pre-empting command ran — if the recovery it interrupted
528:                 // is still owed and nothing else took the stage, re-enter it.
529:                 if let Some((uri, pos)) = self.recovery.take() {
530:                     if self.current.is_none() {
531:                         self.recover_into(uri, pos);
532:                     }
533:                 }
534:             }
535:         }
536:         self.teardown();
537:     }
538: 
539:     /// The per-tick (100 ms) bookkeeping: EOF, health, position.
540:     fn tick(&mut self) {
541:         // Collect the EOF flag under the borrow, then act on it after the
542:         // borrow of `current` is released (`track_ended` needs `&mut self`).
543:         let mut ended = false;
544:         if let Some(cur) = self.current.as_mut() {
545:             let f = cur.frames.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
546:             if f != self.last_seen_frames {
547:                 self.last_seen_frames = f;
548:                 if let Ok(mut h) = self.health.lock() {
549:                     h.last_progress = Instant::now();
550:                 }
551:             }
552:             // Track end: rodio fired the sound-done signal.
553:             ended = cur.done.try_recv().is_ok();
554:             if !ended && self.state.playing && self.last_correction.elapsed() >= POSITION_EVERY {
555:                 // Derive the position from `cur` directly (no `&self` borrow
556:                 // while `current` is mutably borrowed).
557:                 let frames = cur.frames.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
558:                 let pos = frames_to_position(cur.position_ms, frames);
559:                 let uri = cur.uri.clone();
560:                 let _ = self.events.send(EngineEvent::PositionCorrection {
561:                     uri,
562:                     position_ms: pos,
563:                 });
564:                 self.last_correction = Instant::now();
565:             }
566:         }
567:         if ended {
568:             self.track_ended();
569:         }
570:     }
571: 
572:     fn set_health(&mut self, playing: bool) {
573:         if let Ok(mut h) = self.health.lock() {
574:             h.playing = playing;
575:             h.last_progress = Instant::now();
576:         }
577:     }
578: 
579:     fn set_active(&self, active: bool) {
580:         if let Ok(mut b) = self.bands.lock() {
581:             b.is_active = active;
582:         }
583:     }
584: 
585:     fn reset_bands(&self) {
586:         if let Ok(mut b) = self.bands.lock() {
587:             b.values.fill(0.0);
588:             b.peak_envelope = 1e-6;
589:             b.updated_at = Instant::now();
590:         }
591:     }
592: 
593:     fn handle(&mut self, cmd: Cmd) {
594:         match cmd {
595:             Cmd::Load {
596:                 tracks,
597:                 start_uri,
598:                 position_ms,
599:                 shuffle,
600:             } => {
601:                 self.shutdown_current();
602:                 // A fresh context supersedes any in-flight recovery.
603:                 self.recovery = None;
604:                 let start = start_uri
605:                     .as_deref()
606:                     .and_then(|u| tracks.iter().position(|t| t == u))
607:                     .unwrap_or(0);
608:                 if let Ok(mut q) = self.queue_snapshot.lock() {
609:                     *q = tracks.clone();
610:                 }
611:                 self.state = PlayerState {
612:                     // `start` is the cursor: advance picks up after the first
613:                     // track, and history grows from it — not from 0.
614:                     tracks,
615:                     cursor: start,
616:                     history: Vec::new(),
617:                     shuffle,
618:                     repeat: self.state.repeat,
619:                     volume: self.state.volume,
620:                     playing: true,
621:                 };
622:                 self.start_track_at(start, position_ms);
623:             }
624:             Cmd::Resume => {
625:                 if !self.state.playing && self.current.is_none() {
626:                     // Resume from the pause stash: restart the decoder on the
627:                     // same already-resolved URL — no network re-resolve. The
628:                     // stash is taken (cleared) on every outcome so a failed
629:                     // restart can never resurrect it.
630:                     let Some(p) = self.paused.take() else {
631:                         return;
632:                     };
633:                     let pos = truncate_seconds(p.position_ms);
634:                     match self.restart_stream(&p.url, &p.uri, p.duration_ms, pos, true) {
635:                         Ok(()) => {
636:                             self.state.playing = true;
637:                             self.set_health(true);
638:                             self.set_active(true);
639:                             // A fresh post-resume decoder starts with a clean
640:                             // slate, like seek_now and start_track_at give it —
641:                             // the pre-pause streak must not count against it.
642:                             self.drop_streak = 0;
643:                             let _ = self.events.send(EngineEvent::Playing {
644:                                 uri: p.uri,
645:                                 position_ms: pos,
646:                             });
647:                         }
648:                         Err(e) => {
649:                             liblog(format!("engine: resume failed: {e}"));
650:                             // `state.playing` is false while paused, so the
651:                             // rebuild stays paused; after RECOVERY_ATTEMPTS
652:                             // give_up_on skips the track — the audit's
653:                             // prescribed fallback, recover_into unchanged.
654:                             self.recover_into(p.uri, pos);
655:                         }
656:                     }
657:                 } else if !self.state.playing && self.current.is_some() {
658:                     self.player.play();
659:                     self.state.playing = true;
660:                     self.set_health(true);
661:                     self.set_active(true);
662:                     let (uri, pos) = self.current_ident();
663:                     let _ = self.events.send(EngineEvent::Playing {
664:                         uri,
665:                         position_ms: pos,
666:                     });
667:                 }
668:             }
669:             Cmd::Pause => {
670:                 if self.state.playing && self.current.is_some() {
671:                     self.player.pause();
672:                     self.state.playing = false;
673:                     self.set_health(false);
674:                     self.set_active(false);
675:                     let (uri, pos) = self.current_ident();
676:                     let _ = self.events.send(EngineEvent::Paused {
677:                         uri,
678:                         position_ms: pos,
679:                     });
680:                     // Stash the resolved stream, then tear it down: ffmpeg and
681:                     // its googlevideo connection must not stay resident for the
682:                     // whole pause. Resume restarts from this stashed URL — no
683:                     // re-resolve.
684:                     if let Some(cur) = &self.current {
685:                         self.paused = Some(PausedTrack {
686:                             uri: cur.uri.clone(),
687:                             url: cur.url.clone(),
688:                             duration_ms: cur.duration_ms,
689:                             position_ms: pos,
690:                         });
691:                     }
692:                     self.shutdown_current();
693:                 }
694:             }
695:             Cmd::Toggle => {
696:                 if self.state.playing {
697:                     self.handle(Cmd::Pause);
698:                 } else {
699:                     self.handle(Cmd::Resume);
700:                 }
701:             }
702:             Cmd::Next => self.advance(),
703:             Cmd::Prev => {
704:                 // The stash counts as the current track: the >5s restart rule
705:                 // and the no-history restart-at-0 both apply to a paused
706:                 // track too (seek_now updates the stash, staying paused).
707:                 let pos = self.current_pos();
708:                 if (self.current.is_some() || self.paused.is_some()) && pos > 5_000 {
709:                     self.seek_now(0);
710:                 } else if let Some(prev) = self.state.history.pop() {
711:                     self.start_track_at(prev, 0);
712:                 } else if self.current.is_some() || self.paused.is_some() {
713:                     self.seek_now(0);
714:                 }
715:             }
716:             Cmd::Seek(pos) => self.seek_now(pos),
717:             Cmd::Volume(v) => {
718:                 self.state.volume = v;
719:                 self.player.set_volume(v);
720:             }
721:             Cmd::Shuffle(on) => self.state.shuffle = on,
722:             Cmd::Repeat(on) => self.state.repeat = on,
723:             Cmd::Append(uris) => {
724:                 if let Ok(mut q) = self.queue_snapshot.lock() {
725:                     q.extend(uris.iter().cloned());
726:                 }
727:                 self.state.tracks.extend(uris);
728:             }
729:             Cmd::Stop => self.stop_playback(),
730:             Cmd::Recover => self.recover(),
731:         }
732:     }
733: 
734:     /// The canonical identity of the current track, for events.
735:     fn current_ident(&self) -> (String, u32) {
736:         match &self.current {
737:             Some(c) => (c.uri.clone(), self.position_of(c)),
738:             None => (String::new(), 0),
739:         }
740:     }
741: 
742:     fn position_of(&self, cur: &CurrentTrack) -> u32 {
743:         let frames = cur.frames.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
744:         frames_to_position(cur.position_ms, frames)
745:     }
746: 
747:     fn current_pos(&self) -> u32 {
748:         match &self.current {
749:             Some(c) => self.position_of(c),
750:             // While paused the stash owns the playhead: `prev` consults it so
751:             // the pre-teardown contract (restart the current track at 0 when
752:             // past 5s, stay paused) survives the teardown.
753:             None => self.paused.as_ref().map_or(0, |p| p.position_ms),
754:         }
755:     }
756: 
757:     /// Move to the next track in the (possibly shuffled) queue; `None` when
758:     /// the queue is exhausted and repeat is off.
759:     fn advance_index(&mut self) -> Option<usize> {
760:         let n = self.state.tracks.len();
761:         if n == 0 {
762:             return None;
763:         }
764:         if self.state.shuffle && n > 1 {
765:             use rand::Rng as _;
766:             let other: Vec<usize> = (0..n).filter(|&i| i != self.state.cursor).collect();
767:             let pick = other[rand::rng().random_range(0..other.len())];
768:             self.state.history.push(self.state.cursor);
769:             self.state.cursor = pick;
770:             return Some(pick);
771:         }
772:         if self.state.cursor + 1 < n {
773:             self.state.history.push(self.state.cursor);
774:             self.state.cursor += 1;
775:             return Some(self.state.cursor);
776:         }
777:         if self.state.repeat {
778:             self.state.history.push(self.state.cursor);
779:             self.state.cursor = 0;
780:             return Some(0);
781:         }
782:         None
783:     }
784: 
785:     /// `next` (or the natural end of a finished track) — the shared body.
786:     fn advance(&mut self) {
787:         if self.current.is_none() && self.state.tracks.is_empty() {
788:             return;
789:         }
790:         match self.advance_index() {
791:             Some(idx) => self.start_track_at(idx, 0),
792:             None => {
793:                 // Queue over, repeat off: stop cleanly, like the old endpoint. The loaded
794:                 // queue is kept — prev/next still navigate the list after a stop.
795:                 self.shutdown_current();
796:                 self.stop_tail();
797:             }
798:         }
799:     }
800: 
801:     /// The natural end of the current track (EOF): advance the queue; if the
802:     /// process died instead of ending, rebuild the stream.
803:     ///
804:     /// A dropped stream is *not* an end of track: YouTube's transport (and
805:     /// this box's Wi-Fi, verified 2026-08-16) closes the connection mid-song,
806:     /// ffmpeg then exits cleanly (code 0) and the pipe EOFs with only seconds
807:     /// of audio delivered. Without this check the engine would treat that as
808:     /// a finished track and advance/stop. Anything that "ended" in under
809:     /// [`MIN_EOF_POSITION_MS`] of delivered playhead is treated as a failed
810:     /// stream and rebuilt — except when the *track itself* is that short
811:     /// (`duration_ms` says its real end was reached), which is a genuine EOF.
812:     ///
813:     /// Rebuilds are bounded by [`RECOVERY_ATTEMPTS`]: each drop on the same track
814:     /// counts up and the track is given up on (skipped/stopped) once the
815:     /// streak passes, so a persistently-dead stream can't churn forever.
816:     fn track_ended(&mut self) {
817:         let Some(mut cur) = self.current.take() else {
818:             return;
819:         };
820:         let uri = cur.uri.clone();
821:         let pos = self.position_of(&cur);
822:         let failed = cur
823:             .child
824:             .try_wait()
825:             .ok()
826:             .flatten()
827:             .is_some_and(|s| s.code() != Some(0));
828:         let short_track = cur
829:             .duration_ms
830:             .is_some_and(|d| pos.saturating_add(3_000) >= d);
831:         let dropped = !failed && pos < MIN_EOF_POSITION_MS && !short_track;
832:         if failed || dropped {
833:             let _ = cur.child.kill();
834:             let _ = cur.child.wait();
835:             self.drop_streak += 1;
836:             if self.drop_streak >= RECOVERY_ATTEMPTS {
837:                 liblog(format!(
838:                     "engine: giving up on {uri} after {RECOVERY_ATTEMPTS} consecutive failed EOFs"
839:                 ));
840:                 self.give_up_on(uri);
841:                 return;
842:             }
843:             if dropped {
844:                 liblog(format!(
845:                     "engine: stream dropped for {uri} at {pos}ms (<{MIN_EOF_POSITION_MS}ms); rebuilding"
846:                 ));
847:             } else {
848:                 liblog(format!("engine: decoder died for {uri}; rebuilding stream"));
849:             }
850:             self.recover_into(uri, pos);
851:             return;
852:         }
853:         self.drop_streak = 0;
854:         drop(cur);
855:         self.advance();
856:     }
857: 
858:     /// The track is given up on after too many consecutive failures: remove it
859:     /// from the queue (keeping the queue view mirror in sync) and play its
860:     /// successor — or stop cleanly when the queue is over and repeat is off,
861:     /// mirroring `advance()`'s queue-exhausted behavior.
862:     fn give_up_on(&mut self, uri: String) {
863:         self.recovery = None;
864:         self.drop_streak = 0;
865:         let dead = self.state.cursor;
866:         if dead < self.state.tracks.len() && self.state.tracks[dead] == uri {
867:             self.state.tracks.remove(dead);
868:         } else {
869:             self.state.tracks.retain(|t| *t != uri);
870:         }
871:         // History indices shift past the removed slot.
872:         self.state.history.retain(|&h| h != dead);
873:         for h in &mut self.state.history {
874:             if *h > dead {
875:                 *h -= 1;
876:             }
877:         }
878:         *self.queue_snapshot.lock().unwrap() = self.state.tracks.clone();
879:         liblog(format!(
880:             "engine: giving up on {uri} after {RECOVERY_ATTEMPTS} consecutive failed EOFs"
881:         ));
882:         if self.state.tracks.is_empty() {
883:             self.stop_tail();
884:         } else if dead < self.state.tracks.len() {
885:             self.start_track_at(dead, 0);
886:         } else if self.state.repeat {
887:             self.start_track_at(0, 0);
888:         } else {
889:             self.stop_tail();
890:         }
891:     }
892: 
893:     /// A watchdog stall or a failing decoder: re-resolve and restart from the
894:     /// current position, with the old 5–120 s backoff. Gives up (skips the
895:     /// track) after [`RECOVERY_ATTEMPTS`].
896:     fn recover(&mut self) {
897:         let (uri, pos) = self.current_ident();
898:         if uri.is_empty() {
899:             // A recovery in flight owns the uri even while `current` is gone.
900:             if let Some((uri, pos)) = self.recovery.clone() {
901:                 self.recover_into(uri, pos);
902:             }
903:             return;
904:         }
905:         self.recover_into(uri, pos);
906:     }
907: 
908:     fn recover_into(&mut self, uri: String, pos: u32) {
909:         self.shutdown_current();
910:         self.set_health(false); // watchdog off while we rebuild
911:                                 // A paused player stays paused: the stalled stream is rebuilt into
912:                                 // the state it left behind, never force-played.
913:         let play = self.state.playing;
914:         self.recovery = Some((uri.clone(), pos));
915: 
916:         let mut backoff = RETRY_MIN;
917:         for attempt in 0..RECOVERY_ATTEMPTS {
918:             if attempt > 0 {
919:                 let _ = self.events.send(EngineEvent::Reconnecting);
920:             }
921:             match self.build_stream(&uri, pos, play) {
922:                 Ok(()) => {
923:                     if attempt > 0 {
924:                         let _ = self.events.send(EngineEvent::Reconnected);
925:                     }
926:                     self.recovery = None;
927:                     return;
928:                 }
929:                 Err(e) => {

1027:     fn restart_stream(

1070:     /// Resolve `uri`, spawn ffmpeg, append the source and announce Playing — or,

1073:     fn build_stream(&mut self, uri: &str, pos: u32, play: bool) -> Result<()> {
1074:         let resolved = self.expander.resolve(uri).map_err(|e| anyhow!(e))?;

1109:     /// Seek: restart the decoder at `pos` on the current stream URL.

1114:         if let Some(p) = self.paused.as_mut() {

1166: /// Spawn ffmpeg decoding `url` into raw stereo s16 at 44.1 kHz on stdout,
1167: /// seeking to `pos` first (input seek — fast). Returns the child (for
1168: /// kill/reap) plus its stdout, which is where the PCM comes from.
1169: fn spawn_ffmpeg(url: &str, pos: u32) -> Result<(Child, std::process::ChildStdout)> {
1170:     let bin = crate::config::get().ffmpeg_path.clone();
1171:     let mut cmd = Command::new(&bin);
1172:     cmd.args(["-v", "error", "-hide_banner", "-nostdin"]);
1173:     if pos > 0 {
1174:         cmd.arg("-ss").arg(format!("{}", pos / 1000));
1175:     }
1176:     cmd.arg("-i")
1177:         .arg(url)
1178:         .args([
1179:             "-map", "0:a:0", "-vn", "-f", "s16le", "-ac", "2", "-ar", "44100", "-",
1180:         ])
1181:         .stdin(Stdio::null())
1182:         .stderr(Stdio::null())
1183:         .stdout(Stdio::piped())
1184:         .env("FFMPEG_NO_AUTO_CPU_FLAGS", "1");
1185:     let mut child = cmd.spawn().context("spawn ffmpeg")?;
1186:     // Catch an immediate self-exit (bad URL, missing lib) — the pipe would
1187:     // otherwise read EOF immediately and look like a two-sample track.
1188:     if let Some(status) = child.try_wait().ok().flatten() {
1189:         return Err(anyhow!("ffmpeg exited immediately: {status}"));
1190:     }
1191:     let stdout = child.stdout.take().expect("ffmpeg stdout piped");
1192:     Ok((child, stdout))
1193: }

1195: /// Position derivation, pure for testing: `start_ms + frames / 44.1`.
1196: /// Saturating: hostile frame counts clamp to the position ceiling instead of
1197: /// wrapping (u64::MAX × 1000 overflows a u64).
1198: fn frames_to_position(start_ms: u32, frames: u64) -> u32 {
1199:     (start_ms as u64)
1200:         .saturating_add(frames.saturating_mul(1000) / 44_100)
1201:         .min(u32::MAX as u64) as u32
1202: }

1204: /// Whole-second truncation for `-ss` seeks: the decoder starts at the
1205: /// truncated offset, so the playhead anchor, the stash and every position
1206: /// event must agree on it.
1207: fn truncate_seconds(pos: u32) -> u32 {
1208:     pos / 1000 * 1000
1209: }

1214:     let mut image = None;

1230:         image_url: r.thumbnail.clone(),

1233:     }

1236: /// Cover bytes, from disk when they've been seen before; error pages are
1237: /// never cached (identical policy to the api-layer fetch_cover).
1238: fn fetch_cover(client: &reqwest::blocking::Client, url: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
1239:     if let Some(bytes) = crate::httpcache::get_bytes(url) {
1240:         return Some(bytes);
1241:     }
1242:     let resp = client.get(url).send().ok()?;
1243:     if !resp.status().is_success() {
1244:         liblog(format!("cover: {url} -> HTTP {}", resp.status().as_u16()));
1245:         return None;
1246:     }
1247:     let bytes = resp.bytes().ok()?.to_vec();
1248:     crate::httpcache::put_bytes(url, &bytes);
1249:     Some(bytes)
1250: }

3: //! Everything the engine plays arrives as an opaque URI (`yt:video:…`); the

7: //!

9: //!   `spotify:` tracks through the Web API + YouTube search, so the mid-port
10: //!   app stays playable while the api layer still produces Spotify URIs.
11: //! - [`YtExpander`]: pure YouTube — the permanent end state, and what

25: /// One resolved, playable track: the direct stream URL plus the metadata that

27: #[derive(Clone)]
28: pub struct ResolvedTrack {

42: /// Turns a user-facing URI into a flat play queue of playable track uris,
43: /// resolves each to a stream, and seeds radio stations.
44: pub trait Expander: Send + Sync {
45:     /// Expand `uri` into the flat list of track uris it represents, in play
46:     /// order. A bare track passes through as itself; playlists/albums/artists
47:     /// expand into their tracks. Errors are user-facing ("couldn't play…").

49:

51:     /// with). Called from the engine's worker thread for every track start.

53: 
54:     /// The radio station for a seed track: the seed followed by similar uris.

56:     /// deadline fires; the yt-dlp chain stops spawning children instead of
57:     /// running its full fallback for ~40s after the UI has given up.
58:     fn radio(&self, seed: &str, cancel: Arc<AtomicBool>) -> Result<Vec<String>, String>;
59: }

66: impl Expander for YtExpander {
67:     fn expand(&self, uri: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
68:         let Some(("yt", kind, id)) = uri_parts(uri) else {
69:             return Err(format!("not a YouTube uri: {uri}"));
70:         };
71:         let uris = match kind {
72:             "video" => vec![uri.to_string()],
73:             // Playlists / channels / albums all resolve through the one
74:             // kind table in yt; YouTube has no first-class albums — a
75:             // search-backed expansion is the honest approximation.
76:             kind => yt::resolve_kind(kind, id, config::get().search_limit)
77:                 .into_iter()
78:                 .map(|v| v.uri)
79:                 .collect(),
80:         };
81:         if uris.is_empty() {
82:             return Err(format!("{uri} expanded to nothing"));
83:         }
84:         Ok(uris)
85:     }

88:         let Some(id) = track_id_from_uri(uri) else {
89:             return Err(format!("not a track uri: {uri}"));
90:         };
91:         yt::resolve(&id)
92:             .map(ResolvedTrack::from)
93:             .ok_or_else(|| format!("couldn't resolve {uri}"))

96:     fn radio(&self, seed: &str, cancel: Arc<AtomicBool>) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
97:         let Some(id) = track_id_from_uri(seed) else {
98:             return Err(format!("not a track uri: {seed}"));
99:         };
100:         // `radio_entries` caps the mix fetch to one inner-page (a full RD mix
101:         // paginates 15+ API calls and blows past the app's radio deadline),
102:         // falls back across the mix id variants, and ends in a search-built
103:         // pseudo-radio when YouTube has no mix for the seed at all. `cancel`
104:         // (F13) is checked between every chain step and inside yt_stdout's
105:         // poll loop, so a timed-out request kills its children in-flight.
106:         let rows = yt::radio_entries(&id, cancel);
107:         station_from(seed, rows)
108:     }

111: /// The seed first, then the mix rows — the seed itself skipped when the mix
112: /// echoes it, the whole list capped to `RADIO_LIMIT` + 1. Pure (no network), so
113: /// the station-shape logic is unit-tested offline; only the mix fetch is live.
114: fn station_from(seed: &str, rows: Vec<yt::YtVideo>) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
115:     let mut uris = vec![seed.to_string()];
116:     for row in rows.into_iter().take(RADIO_LIMIT) {
117:         if row.uri != seed {
118:             uris.push(row.uri);
119:         }
120:     }
121:     if uris.len() == 1 {
122:         return Err(format!("radio station for {seed} came back empty"));
123:     }
124:     Ok(uris)
125: }

255:         }

1: # Backend inspiration: DominatorMusic
2: 
3: Reading this created zero adopted code — everything below is a transferable idea,
4: checked against Tuna TUI's own constraints. The project itself is GPL-3.0, so any
5: actual code copying would be a licensing problem; these are *patterns*, noted so

7: 
8: **Source:** [DominatorMusic (DominatorStufs)](https://github.com/DominatorStufs/DominatorMusic)
9: — an Android music player streaming from YouTube Music, fork of Vitune. Inspected 2026-08-16.
10: 
11: ## What it does, at a glance
12: 
13: - Playback from **YouTube Music** through *multiple swappable providers*:
14:   `providers/{innertube, piped, kugou, lrclib, sponsorblock, …}`.
15: - Lyrics from **lrclib.net** — the same lrclib Tuna TUI already uses.
16: - Radio via **watch-mix** (`RD` playlists) — the same radio concept Tuna TUI `YtExpander` uses.
17: - Offline cache, background playback, playlist import, mood/genre discovery.
18: 
19: ## Ideas worth borrowing (each with Tuna TUI status)
20: 
21: ### 1. Provider-as-trait (already done here)
22: They ship several transports behind one interface so a dead backend can be
23: swapped without touching the UI. Tuna TUI's `Expander` (`src/engine/expander.rs`)
24: is exactly this shape: `YtExpander` (yt-dlp today), and the deleted
25: `HybridExpander` proved a second implementation could coexist. **Status: done.**
26: 
27: ### 2. Direct InnerTube as a yt-dlp alternative (a future option)
28: Their `providers/innertube` talks to `https://youtubei.googleapis.com/youtubei/v1/…`
29: directly — search, browse, player, next, with a `JavaScriptChallenge.kt` for the
30: signature (n-sig) dance yt-dlp does in-process.
31: 
32: Why it matters for Tuna TUI: the standing maintenance surface of the port is yt-dlp
33: breaking (po-token/bot checks, throttled streams). A direct-InnerTube transport
34: would drop the CLI + ffmpeg dependency and give typed responses. The cost is
35: real: the JS challenge solver is the kind of thing that breaks weekly, which is
36: precisely why we chose a mature binary instead. **Not now — but the Expander
37: trait means this is a *drop-in* later, not a rewrite.** The `cookies_file` +
38: retry path stays either way.
39: 
40: ### 3. Radio from the *watch response's* radio playlist — **tested, not adoptable, superseded**
41: Their `NextPage` reads `playlistId` out of the video body (`watch?v=X` →
42: `RD…`) instead of *assuming* `RD<id>`. Tuna TUI **tested this live (2026-08-16) and
43: it does not apply to a yt-dlp-based app**: neither yt-dlp's `-J` watch output
44: nor the watch-page HTML carries the current video's own mix id (the HTML's
45: every `RD…` is a *related* video's `start_radio` command; the panel content is
46: only served by an innertube POST). The `RD<videoId>` convention itself is
47: deterministic and correct.
48: 
49: What the live probes found instead, and what was fixed (bead `Myx-a4e.7`):
50: - **The real radio defect was pagination, not the id**: an un-capped
51:   `--flat-playlist` on a mix walks 15+ sequential innertube pages (~20–27 s on
52:   a healthy network) while the station only keeps 50 rows — the app's 12 s
53:   deadline fired before a single row arrived. Fixed by capping the fetch to one
54:   inner-page (`--playlist-end 40`, ~3.7 s).
55: - **Second latent defect**: fresh/obscure seeds have no mix at all — or their
56:   player endpoint is bot-gated — so the mix candidates return nothing. Fixed
57:   with a fallback chain: `RD<id>` → `RDAMVM<id>` → a **search-built
58:   pseudo-radio** (find the seed's own row via the open search API, then flat-
59:   search its title). Everything in the fallback rides the search API, which is
60:   never gated where the player endpoint is.
61: 
62: ### 4. lrclib best-match with a duration tolerance (small, high-value)
63: Their lrclib provider matches `bestMatchingFor` — a duration window around the
64: track, not an exact `duration=` param. YouTube rows are the *video's* length
65: (often ±2–10s vs the release), which is why Tuna TUI's exact-duration lrclib query
66: occasionally misses a synced lyric that clearly exists. Improvement: query lrclib
67: `/api/search` with the name, then pick the result whose `duration` is within
68: ~10s of the video's, instead of `/api/get?duration=` exact.
69: 
70: ### 5. SponsorBlock (a real feature gap)
71: Their `sponsorblock` provider skips intros/outros/sponsors mid-track. Our engine
72: is a plain stream with a seek command — segment skipping is *already playable*
73: once a sponsorblock lookup exists: on `TrackChanged`, fetch segments, and when
74: `PositionCorrection` crosses a segment boundary, issue `seek`. Behind a config
75: flag. **Filed as a bead (P3), not this phase.**
76: 
77: ### 6. Search suggestions + genre/mood discovery (UI-adjacent)
78: `SearchSuggestions` (type-ahead) and `DiscoverPage` (mood/genre mixes). Tuna TUI's
79: flat `ytsearchN` search is deliberately minimal; suggestions would mean a
80: second autocomplete call per keystroke. **Suggestions filed as a P4 bead;
81: mood/genre discovery reviewed and skipped** (no first-class yt-dlp endpoint).
82: 
83: ### 7. Full gap sweep (2026-08-16, pattern-only)
84: A structured review of the DominatorMusic codebase produced the complete
85: adoption list beyond the sections above — all filed as beads so the analysis
86: isn't lost: **skip-on-error auto-advance** (adopt-now, P2), **SponsorBlock**
87: (§5, P3), **search suggestions** (§6, P4), and a P4 backlog basket holding
88: playback speed/pitch (ffmpeg atempo), persistent queue across restarts,
89: loudness normalization (`normalizedLoudnessDb` → ffmpeg `volume` filter),
90: per-track blacklist, offline cache via `yt-dlp -x`, and YTM-innertube lyrics
91: as a second source + local lyric editing (pairs with the lrclib tolerance
92: work in bead `Myx-a4e.7`). Skipped after review: mood/genre discovery, Piped
93: account sync, Google Translate integration.

95: ## What NOT to take
96: 
97: - The MultiLine "tabs/player/queue" UI architecture — Tuna TUI's UI is deliberately
98:   untouched and ratatui-shaped.
99: - Any actual code — GPL-3.0 provenance; patterns only.

29: /// so lyrics added upstream since the last run are picked up (no
30: /// never-cache-empty trap, no TTL needed).
31: static MEMO: LazyLock<Mutex<HashMap<String, MemoValue>>> =
32:     LazyLock::new(|| Mutex::new(HashMap::new()));

34: /// Fetch lyrics for a track from lrclib. Returns `(lines, synced)`; synced
35: /// lines carry timestamps, plain text has none. An empty first half means no
36: /// match — the caller renders the view empty.
37: pub fn fetch_lyrics_blocking(
38:     artist: &str,
39:     title: &str,
40:     album: &str,
41:     duration_ms: u32,
42: ) -> (Vec<(u32, String)>, bool) {

44:     let url = format!(

46:         urlencode(artist),
47:         urlencode(title),
48:         urlencode(album),

52: }

54: /// The memo wrapper: identical requests (same URL) are served from memory —
55: /// the network legs of [`fetch_lyrics_url`] never run twice for one track in
56: /// one session. The client is injected so tests can point the miss path at an
57: /// offline endpoint without touching the real lrclib.net. Never holds the
58: /// lock across the network fetch (a memo miss must not serialize fetches).
59: fn fetch_lyrics_memo(client: &reqwest::blocking::Client, url: &str) -> (Vec<(u32, String)>, bool) {
60:     if let Some(hit) = MEMO.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner()).get(url) {
61:         return hit.clone();
62:     }
63:     let result = fetch_lyrics_url(client, url);
64:     MEMO.lock()
65:         .unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner())
66:         .insert(url.to_string(), result.clone());

68: }

2: //!
3: //! Spotify's development-mode quota is per app, and it runs out: an artist
4: //! drill-in costs four requests, so a few minutes of browsing can earn a `429`
5: //! with a `Retry-After` measured in hours. Cached bodies keep repeat visits off
6: //! the network entirely, and a stale entry is served when the request fails —
7: //! an album list from yesterday beats an empty page.
8: //!
9: //! Only immutable-ish catalogue data belongs here. Anything the user can change
10: //! (playback state, saved-track flags) must go straight to the API.

41:             let _ = fs::set_permissions(&dir, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o700));
42:         }
43:         sweep(&dir, KEEP);
44:         Some(dir)

49: /// One blocking HTTP client for all small fetches (cover art, lyrics, meta).
50: ///
51: /// The engine and the lyrics fetcher used to each carry this exact builder;
52: /// the timeout is the shared policy — a stalled network must not wedge a
53: /// worker thread forever. The `unwrap_or_default` fallback keeps the
54: /// (unusual) builder failure from taking the whole fetch path down.
55: ///
56: /// Building a blocking client creates — and drops — reqwest's own inner
57: /// runtime, which tokio refuses to do inside a live runtime. The once-cell
58: /// plus [`warm_blocking_client`] (called before the app's runtime starts)
59: /// keeps every later use, engine and lyrics alike, on the ready client.
60: #[cfg(feature = "streaming")]
61: static CLIENT: OnceLock<reqwest::blocking::Client> = OnceLock::new();
62: 
63: #[cfg(feature = "streaming")]
64: pub fn blocking_client() -> &'static reqwest::blocking::Client {
65:     CLIENT.get_or_init(|| {
66:         reqwest::blocking::Client::builder()
67:             .timeout(Duration::from_secs(10))
68:             .build()
69:             .unwrap_or_default()
70:     })
71: }
72: 
73: /// Construct the blocking client eagerly, outside any tokio runtime.
74: /// Idempotent: a later call from inside the runtime is a no-op.
75: #[cfg(feature = "streaming")]
76: pub fn warm_blocking_client() {
77:     let _ = blocking_client();
78: }

80: /// Drop entries nobody has asked for in a month. Runs once, on the first cache
81: /// hit of the session.
82: fn sweep(dir: &Path, keep: Duration) {
83:     let Ok(entries) = fs::read_dir(dir) else {
84:         return;
85:     };
86:     for entry in entries.flatten() {

92:             .is_some_and(|age| age > keep);

95:         }
96:     }
97: }

### visualizer-feed-decoupled-from-playback
Myx 2026-08-16 (Myx-a4e.14): the frozen-visualizer bug root cause — the FFT tee was fed from *delivery* (fold draining the pump channel into pending) not from *playback* (the pops). fold() drained the whole bounded(8) channel greedily; the pump outruns playback (instant local files, bursty network), channel empties, EOF flips, tee goes silent while pending still plays. FIX in src/engine/ffmpeg_source.rs fold(): bounded pull — fold only while pending.len() < PREBUFFER_SAMPLES; delivery paced to playhead, backpressure blocks the pump thread not the callback. rodio side verified: mixer wraps sources in UniformSourceIterator and keeps polling; the queue keeps calling next() while the source returns samples — rodio never stops polling, the source starves itself. Lesson: feed consumer-facing meters (FFT, playhead) from what is SERVED, not what is DELIVERED. Also policy: ALL audio tests must be SILENT — device oracles use player.set_volume(0.0) (user has headphones connected; data path is volume-independent).

### youtube-access-asymmetry-on-this-box-verified-2026
YouTube access asymmetry on this box (verified 2026-08-16): the flat search API (ytsearchN:, --flat-playlist) stays open even when the player endpoint is bot-gated. Fresh/obscure videos get player-level 'Sign in to confirm' gates (video_meta/-J --no-playlist returns rc=1) while search returns them fine. Consequences: (1) any new metadata source should prefer search-by-id over --no-playlist; (2) an empty radio station for fresh seeds is usually a gate, not a missing mix. Myx's radio pseudo-radio fallback already exploits this (src/yt/mod.rs).

66: pub fn ensure_cache_dir_0700() -> Option<PathBuf> {

77: /// A unique temp sibling for [`write_atomic`]. One process-wide counter feeds
78: /// every writer, so two overlapping saves (the un-awaited periodic tick and
79: /// the awaited quit save) can never share a scratch name and rename a torn
80: /// temp into place.
81: fn tmp_sibling(path: &Path) -> PathBuf {
82:     static SEQ: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
83:     path.with_extension(format!("{}.tmp", SEQ.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)))
84: }

86: /// Write `bytes` to `path` atomically: a uniquely-named temp sibling, fsync,
87: /// then rename over the destination. Returns true when the rename landed; on
88: /// any failure the temp is removed and false is returned — a torn write can
89: /// never become the visible file.
90: ///
91: /// The rename-over-existing fallback covers Windows, where the rename can
92: /// fail over a destination that is open or otherwise locked: the destination
93: /// is removed and the rename retried once. The fallback deletes the old file
94: /// before the second rename, so a failure there leaves `path` absent — the
95: /// state.json caller keeps `.bak` to cover the gap; on unix the first rename
96: /// replaces in place and the fallback is effectively unreachable.
97: ///
98: /// `pub` because the persistence caller lives in the binary crate; only the
99: /// lib crate's own modules could see a `pub(crate)` item.
100: pub fn write_atomic(path: &Path, bytes: &[u8]) -> bool {
101:     let tmp = tmp_sibling(path);
102:     if std::fs::File::create(&tmp)
103:         .and_then(|mut f| {
104:             f.write_all(bytes)?;
105:             f.sync_all()
106:         })
107:         .is_err()
108:     {
109:         let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&tmp);

111:     }

113:         return true;
114:     }

116:     // Never run on Unix: a failed first rename fails identically after
117:     // remove, so the destination would be deleted for nothing.
118:     #[cfg(windows)]

120:         if std::fs::remove_file(path).is_ok() && std::fs::rename(&tmp, path).is_ok() {
121:             return true;
122:         }
123:     }
124:     let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&tmp);
125:     false
126: }

151:         ("yt", "video") => video_url(uri).unwrap_or_default(),

153:         ("yt", "channel") => format!("https://www.youtube.com/channel/{id}"),

161: pub fn video_url(url_or_id: &str) -> Option<String> {
162:     if url_or_id.starts_with("http://") || url_or_id.starts_with("https://") {

168:     // A bare id — but only a bare one: a `yt:playlist:` or other non-video uri
169:     // must not masquerade as a video id.
170:     if url_or_id.contains(':') {
171:         return None;
172:     }
173:     (!url_or_id.is_empty()).then(|| format!("https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={url_or_id}"))
174: }
175: 
176: /// The canonical playlist URL.
177: pub fn playlist_uri(id: &str) -> String {
178:     format!("https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list={id}")
179: }
180: 
181: /// The canonical channel uploads tab — what a `yt:channel:` drill-in expands.
182: pub fn channel_videos_url(id: &str) -> String {
183:     format!("https://www.youtube.com/channel/{id}/videos")
184: }
185: 
186: /// Pull the id out of a `yt:video:<id>` URI.
187: pub fn track_id_from_uri(uri: &str) -> Option<String> {
188:     match uri_parts(uri) {
189:         Some(("yt", "video", id)) => Some(id.to_string()),
190:         _ => None,
191:     }
192: }
193: 
194: /// Percent-encode a string for use in a query component.
195: pub fn urlencode(s: &str) -> String {
196:     let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len());
197:     for b in s.bytes() {
198:         match b {
199:             b'A'..=b'Z' | b'a'..=b'z' | b'0'..=b'9' | b'-' | b'_' | b'.' | b'~' => {
200:                 out.push(b as char)
201:             }
202:             _ => out.push_str(&format!("%{b:02X}")),
203:         }
204:     }
205:     out
206: }
