```text
//! Providers — ViTune-compatible backend per implementation_spec.md.
//!
//! `contracts` holds stable domain types (§11, §33, §40, §66).
//! `router` composes them with fallback chains (§50-51).
//! Submodules are adapters; `ytdlp` wraps the existing yt-dlp path as a provider.

pub mod contracts;
pub mod router;
pub mod ytdlp;

pub mod innertube {
    pub mod client;
}
pub mod piped {
    pub mod client;
}
pub mod lrclib {
    pub mod client;
}
pub mod sponsorblock {
    pub mod client;
}

// Re-export for ergonomic use
pub use contracts::{
    AlbumRef, ArtistRef, AudioStream, CircuitBreaker, CircuitState, Lyrics, LyricsQuery,
    PlaybackInfo, Provider, ProviderError, ProviderErrorCode, ProviderId, SearchOptions,
    SearchResultPage, SearchType, Song, SponsorSegment, Thumbnail, VideoStream,
};
pub use router::ProviderRouter;

/// Global router (lazy) — optional for now; engine will own its instance.
/// Kept as OnceLock so browse threads can share without passing Arc everywhere later.
use std::sync::{Arc, OnceLock};

static GLOBAL_ROUTER: OnceLock<Arc<ProviderRouter>> = OnceLock::new();

/// Build the default router: yt-dlp only, innertube/piped stubs disabled by default.
/// This is the "replace existing logic" seam — the old yt::search/resolve calls
/// will be routed through here, so flipping a flag enables the new providers
/// without touching call sites.
pub fn global_router() -> Arc<ProviderRouter> {
    GLOBAL_ROUTER
        .get_or_init(|| {
            let mut r = ProviderRouter::new();
            // yt-dlp is the only healthy provider today. InnerTube/Piped stubs
            // return InstanceUnhealthy and fall through immediately — zero risk.
            r.ytdlp_stream = Some(Arc::new(ytdlp::YtDlpStreamProvider));
            r.ytdlp_search_fallback();
            Arc::new(r)
        })
        .clone()
}

impl ProviderRouter {
    fn ytdlp_search_fallback(&mut self) {
        // Use yt-dlp for search fallback until InnerTube search lands.
        // We keep the type alias so the router field is populated even before
        // the real adapter ships — search() will then succeed via yt-dlp.
        self.innertube_search = Some(Arc::new(ytdlp::YtDlpSearchProvider));
    }
}
```

```text
1: //! The resolver seam between the app and the engine.
2: //!
3: //! Everything the engine plays arrives as an opaque URI (`yt:video:…`); the
4: //! [`Expander`] turns those into direct stream URLs plus the metadata a local
5: //! player needs. Kept behind a trait so the engine never learns a provider's
6: //! scheme:
7: //!
8: //! - Phase 2 (app side, `src/hybrid_expander.rs`, deleted in phase 3): maps
9: //!   `spotify:` tracks through the Web API + YouTube search, so the mid-port
10: //!   app stays playable while the api layer still produces Spotify URIs.
11: //! - [`YtExpander`]: pure YouTube — the permanent end state, and what
12: //!   `examples/probe` drives.
13: //!
14: //! One-way dependency, like `api/`: expansion and resolution spawn the yt-dlp
15: //! CLI and hand plain data back; nothing here touches `App` or the render tree.
16: //! All parse/format logic is offline-testable on canned `-J` JSON (phase 1's
17: //! conventions); live behavior is exercised by `examples/probe`.
18: 
19: use crate::config;
20: use crate::util::{track_id_from_uri, uri_parts};
21: use crate::yt;
22: use std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool;
23: use std::sync::Arc;
24: 
25: /// One resolved, playable track: the direct stream URL plus the metadata that
26: /// playback events and the NowPlaying pipeline consume.
27: #[derive(Clone)]
28: pub struct ResolvedTrack {
29:     /// A direct audio URL, valid for the session (re-resolve on recovery).
30:     pub url: String,
31:     pub title: String,
32:     pub artist: String,
33:     pub album: Option<String>,
34:     pub duration_ms: Option<u32>,
35:     pub thumbnail: Option<String>,
36: }
37: 
38: /// How many radio tracks (besides the seed) a station expands to. Mixes run
39: /// hundreds deep; the app's queue and memory want a sane slice.
40: pub const RADIO_LIMIT: usize = 50;
41: 
42: /// Turns a user-facing URI into a flat play queue of playable track uris,
43: /// resolves each to a stream, and seeds radio stations.
44: pub trait Expander: Send + Sync {
45:     /// Expand `uri` into the flat list of track uris it represents, in play
46:     /// order. A bare track passes through as itself; playlists/albums/artists
47:     /// expand into their tracks. Errors are user-facing ("couldn't play…").
48:     fn expand(&self, uri: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, String>;
49: 
50:     /// Resolve ONE track uri to a direct stream URL (+ the metadata it comes
51:     /// with). Called from the engine's worker thread for every track start.
52:     fn resolve(&self, uri: &str) -> Result<ResolvedTrack, String>;
53: 
54:     /// The radio station for a seed track: the seed followed by similar uris.
55:     /// `cancel` (F13) is the per-request flag set once the app's radio
56:     /// deadline fires; the yt-dlp chain stops spawning children instead of
57:     /// running its full fallback for ~40s after the UI has given up.
58:     fn radio(&self, seed: &str, cancel: Arc<AtomicBool>) -> Result<Vec<String>, String>;
59: }
60: 
61: /// The pure-YouTube expander — the port's end state, live from phase 1's
62: /// `yt/` module.
63: #[derive(Default)]
64: pub struct YtExpander;
65: 
66: impl Expander for YtExpander {
67:     fn expand(&self, uri: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
68:         let Some(("yt", kind, id)) = uri_parts(uri) else {
69:             return Err(format!("not a YouTube uri: {uri}"));
70:         };
71:         let uris = match kind {
72:             "video" => vec![uri.to_string()],
73:             // Playlists / channels / albums all resolve through the one
74:             // kind table in yt; YouTube has no first-class albums — a
75:             // search-backed expansion is the honest approximation.
76:             kind => yt::resolve_kind(kind, id, config::get().search_limit)
77:                 .into_iter()
78:                 .map(|v| v.uri)
79:                 .collect(),
80:         };
81:         if uris.is_empty() {
82:             return Err(format!("{uri} expanded to nothing"));
83:         }
84:         Ok(uris)
85:     }
86: 
87:     fn resolve(&self, uri: &str) -> Result<ResolvedTrack, String> {
88:         let Some(id) = track_id_from_uri(uri) else {
89:             return Err(format!("not a track uri: {uri}"));
90:         };
91:         yt::resolve(&id)
92:             .map(ResolvedTrack::from)
93:             .ok_or_else(|| format!("couldn't resolve {uri}"))
94:     }
95: 
96:     fn radio(&self, seed: &str, cancel: Arc<AtomicBool>) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
97:         let Some(id) = track_id_from_uri(seed) else {
98:             return Err(format!("not a track uri: {seed}"));
99:         };
100:         // `radio_entries` caps the mix fetch to one inner-page (a full RD mix
101:         // paginates 15+ API calls and blows past the app's radio deadline),
102:         // falls back across the mix id variants, and ends in a search-built
103:         // pseudo-radio when YouTube has no mix for the seed at all. `cancel`
104:         // (F13) is checked between every chain step and inside yt_stdout's
105:         // poll loop, so a timed-out request kills its children in-flight.
106:         let rows = yt::radio_entries(&id, cancel);
107:         station_from(seed, rows)
108:     }
109: }
110: 
111: /// The seed first, then the mix rows — the seed itself skipped when the mix
112: /// echoes it, the whole list capped to `RADIO_LIMIT` + 1. Pure (no network), so
113: /// the station-shape logic is unit-tested offline; only the mix fetch is live.
114: fn station_from(seed: &str, rows: Vec<yt::YtVideo>) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
115:     let mut uris = vec![seed.to_string()];
116:     for row in rows.into_iter().take(RADIO_LIMIT) {
117:         if row.uri != seed {
118:             uris.push(row.uri);
119:         }
120:     }
121:     if uris.len() == 1 {
122:         return Err(format!("radio station for {seed} came back empty"));
123:     }
124:     Ok(uris)
125: }
126:

129:         ResolvedTrack {
130:             url: s.url,
131:             title: s.video.title,
132:             artist: s.video.artist,
133:             album: s.video.album,
134:             duration_ms: s.video.duration_ms,
135:             thumbnail: s.video.thumbnail,
136:         }
137:     }
138: }
```

```text
21: /// done signal anymore — nothing can fail at the transport, an empty store is
22: /// a legitimate (fresh) state, and the reload path re-spawns with a fresh
23: /// store snapshot. (The app clears its loading status once the last section
24: /// of a drain lands.)
25: pub(crate) fn spawn_library_fetch(store: Store, tx: flume::Sender<(Section, Vec<LibItem>)>) {
26:     std::thread::Builder::new()
27:         .name("tuna-library".to_string())
28:         .spawn(move || build_sections(&store, tx))
29:         .expect("spawn library worker");
30: }
31: 
32: fn build_sections(store: &Store, tx: flume::Sender<(Section, Vec<LibItem>)>) {
33:     // Home: a rolling mix of recently played and most-played tracks.
34:     let mut home: Vec<LibItem> = Vec::new();
35:     if store.history.is_empty() {
36:         home.push(LibItem::header("nothing played yet — search for a song"));
37:     } else {
38:         home.push(LibItem::header("Recently Played"));
39:         home.extend(history_rows(store.history.iter()).take(6));
40:         let mut top: Vec<&PlayedEntry> = store.history.iter().collect();
41:         top.sort_by(|a, b| b.count.cmp(&a.count).then(b.last_ms.cmp(&a.last_ms)));
42:         home.push(LibItem::header("Top Tracks"));
43:         home.extend(history_rows(top.into_iter()).take(8));
44:     }
45:     let _ = tx.send((Section::Home, home));
46: 
47:     let recent: Vec<LibItem> = history_rows(store.history.iter()).take(50).collect();
48:     let _ = tx.send((Section::Recent, recent));
49: 
50:     let playlists: Vec<LibItem> = store
51:         .playlists
52:         .iter()
53:         .map(|p| {
54:             let subtitle = if p.subtitle.is_empty() {
55:                 format!("{} saved", p.tracks.len())
56:             } else {
57:                 p.subtitle.clone()
58:             };
59:             LibItem::ctx(p.name.clone(), subtitle, p.uri.clone())
60:         })
61:         .collect();
62:     let _ = tx.send((Section::Playlists, playlists));
63: 
64:     let albums: Vec<LibItem> = store
65:         .albums
66:         .iter()
67:         .map(|a| LibItem::ctx(a.name.clone(), a.subtitle.clone(), a.uri.clone()))
68:         .collect();
69:     let _ = tx.send((Section::Albums, albums));
70: 
71:     let artists: Vec<LibItem> = store
72:         .artists
73:         .iter()
74:         .map(|a| LibItem::ctx(a.name.clone(), String::new(), a.uri.clone()))
75:         .collect();
76:     let _ = tx.send((Section::Artists, artists));
77: 
78:     // Liked keeps its synthetic play row and header, matching the old shape.
79:     let mut liked: Vec<LibItem> = vec![
80:         LibItem::play(
81:             "▶︎  Play Liked Songs".into(),
82:             "tuna:action:liked-play".into(),
83:         ),
84:         LibItem::header("Songs"),
85:     ];
86:     liked.extend(
87:         store
88:             .liked
89:             .iter()
90:             .map(|e| LibItem::track(e.name.clone(), e.subtitle.clone(), e.uri.clone())),
91:     );
92:     let _ = tx.send((Section::Liked, liked));
93: }
94: 
95: /// Search: `ytsearchN:` flat results, rendered as Songs rows. There are no
96: /// first-class YouTube artist/album/playlist entities to group — the other
97: /// groups die with the Spotify search schema.
98: pub(crate) fn spawn_search(query: String, tx: flume::Sender<Vec<LibItem>>) {
99:     std::thread::Builder::new()
100:         .name("tuna-search".to_string())
101:         .spawn(move || {
102:             let vids = yt::search(&query, config::get().search_limit);
103:             let mut out = Vec::new();
104:             if !vids.is_empty() {
105:                 out.push(LibItem::header("Songs"));
106:             }
107:             out.extend(
108:                 vids.into_iter()
109:                     .map(|v| LibItem::track(v.title, v.artist, v.uri)),
110:             );
111:             let _ = tx.send(out);
112:         })
113:         .expect("spawn search worker");
114: }
115: 
116: /// Drill into a context (playlist / channel / album / single video). The
117: /// response tuple `(context_uri, title, items)` matches the old fetch.
118: pub(crate) fn spawn_detail_fetch(
119:     store: Store,
120:     uri: String,
121:     name: String,
122:     tx: flume::Sender<(String, String, Vec<LibItem>)>,
123: ) {
124:     std::thread::Builder::new()
125:         .name("tuna-detail".to_string())
126:         .spawn(move || {
127:             let (title, items) = fetch_detail_blocking(&store, &uri, &name);
128:             let _ = tx.send((uri, title, items));
129:         })
130:         .expect("spawn detail worker");
131: }
132: 
133: pub(crate) fn fetch_detail_blocking(
134:     store: &Store,
135:     uri: &str,
136:     name: &str,
137: ) -> (String, Vec<LibItem>) {
138:     // "Play all" row first.
139:     let mut items = vec![LibItem::play(format!("▶︎ Play {name}"), uri.to_string())];
140: 
141:     let (_, kind, id) = match uri_parts(uri) {
142:         Some(p) => p,
143:         None => return (name.to_string(), items),
144:     };
145: 
146:     match kind {
147:         // A playlist whose contents have grown locally renders its own rows;
148:         // otherwise the network copy (flat-extracted) is the contents.
149:         // (No `if let` match guard: unstable E0658 on the current toolchain.)
150:         "playlist" => {
151:             // Prefer the local rows when the store has them.
152:             if let Some(rows) = store.playlist_tracks(uri) {
153:                 append_or_hint(
154:                     &mut items,
155:                     rows.iter()
156:                         .map(|t| LibItem::track(t.name.clone(), t.subtitle.clone(), t.uri.clone())),
157:                     "empty playlist",
158:                 );
159:                 return (name.to_string(), items);
160:             }
161:             // Capped (F14): the drill-in view must not paginate a whole
162:             // multi-hundred-row playlist. Deliberately NOT `search_limit`
163:             // (defaults to 6 — would truncate a 30-track playlist with no
164:             // hint) and NOT `resolve_kind`: that table feeds the PLAY path,
165:             // which must stay un-capped (bead Myx-a4.8).
166:             append_or_hint(
167:                 &mut items,
168:                 kind_rows(&yt::playlist_entries_capped(
169:                     &tuna_tui::util::playlist_uri(id),
170:                     yt::DRILLIN_FETCH_LIMIT,
171:                 )),
172:                 "no tracks — empty or restricted",
173:             );
174:         }
175:         "channel" => {
176:             append_or_hint(
177:                 &mut items,
178:                 kind_rows(&yt::playlist_entries_capped(
179:                     &tuna_tui::util::channel_videos_url(id),
180:                     yt::DRILLIN_FETCH_LIMIT,
181:                 )),
182:                 "no uploads — empty or restricted",
183:             );
184:         }
185:         "album" => {
186:             // YouTube has no first-class albums; the saved slug searches.
187:             append_or_hint(
188:                 &mut items,
189:                 yt::resolve_kind(kind, id, config::get().search_limit)
190:                     .into_iter()
191:                     .map(|v| LibItem::track(v.title, v.artist, v.uri)),
192:                 "nothing loaded — search failed",
193:             );
194:         }
195:         "video" => {
196:             append_or_hint(
197:                 &mut items,
198:                 yt::video_meta(id)
199:                     .into_iter()
200:                     .map(|v| LibItem::track(v.title, v.artist, v.uri)),
201:                 "couldn't load — check the network",
202:             );
203:         }
204:         _ => {}
205:     }
206: 
207:     (name.to_string(), items)
208: }
209: 
210: /// Extend `items` with `rows`; when the source yielded nothing (an empty or
211: /// restricted playlist, a failed search), push a header `hint` instead.
212: /// Returns whether rows were added.
213: fn append_or_hint(
214:     items: &mut Vec<LibItem>,
215:     rows: impl IntoIterator<Item = LibItem>,
216:     hint: &str,
217: ) -> bool {
218:     let before = items.len();
219:     items.extend(rows);
220:     if items.len() == before {
221:         items.push(LibItem::header(hint));
222:         false
223:     } else {
224:         true
225:     }
226: }
227: 
228: /// The history rows shared by Home's Recently Played / Top Tracks and the
229: /// Recent section — one mapping so `PlayedEntry`'s shape stays in sync
230: /// everywhere it renders.
231: fn history_rows<'a>(
232:     rows: impl Iterator<Item = &'a PlayedEntry> + 'a,
233: ) -> impl Iterator<Item = LibItem> + 'a {
234:     rows.map(|h| LibItem::track(h.title.clone(), h.artist.clone(), h.uri.clone()))
235: }
236: 
237: /// Playlist / channel rows in local style: flat entries are title-only —
238: /// split "Artist - Title (…)" so the list isn't long pasted strings.
239: fn kind_rows(rows: &[yt::YtVideo]) -> Vec<LibItem> {
240:     rows.iter()
241:         .map(|v| {
242:             let (name, subtitle) = title_artist_split(&v.title);
243:             LibItem::track(name, subtitle, v.uri.clone())
244:         })
245:         .collect()
246: }
247: 
248: /// Split a YouTube title at a power-separator: "Artist - Title (Official
249: /// Video)" → ("Title (Official Video)", "Artist"). Falls back to the whole
250: /// string (subtitle empty) when no separator exists.
251: fn title_artist_split(s: &str) -> (String, String) {
252:     for sep in [" – ", " - ", " — ", "-"] {
253:         if let Some((artist, title)) = s.split_once(sep) {
254:             return (title.trim().to_string(), artist.trim().to_string());
255:         }
256:     }
257:     (s.to_string(), String::new())
258: }
259: 
260: #[cfg(test)]
261: mod tests {
262:     use super::*;
263: 
264:     #[test]
265:     fn split_pulls_artist_and_title_around_dashes() {
266:         assert_eq!(
267:             title_artist_split("Queen – Bohemian Rhapsody (Official Video Remastered)"),
268:             (
269:                 "Bohemian Rhapsody (Official Video Remastered)".to_string(),
270:                 "Queen".to_string()
271:             )
272:         );
273:         assert_eq!(
274:             title_artist_split("Survivor - Eye Of The Tiger (Official HD Video)"),
275:             (
276:                 "Eye Of The Tiger (Official HD Video)".to_string(),
277:                 "Survivor".to_string()
278:             )
279:         );
280:         assert_eq!(
281:             title_artist_split("Some Plain Podcast Episode"),
282:             ("Some Plain Podcast Episode".to_string(), String::new())
283:         );
284:         // No double-split: "A - B - C" takes the first separator only.
285:         assert_eq!(
286:             title_artist_split("A - B - C"),
287:             ("B - C".to_string(), "A".to_string())
288:         );
289:     }
290:

313:

315:     fn home_builds_recent_and_top_from_history() {
```

````text
1: # ViTune-Compatible Music Backend — Implementation Specification
2: 
3: > **Purpose:** Implement a server-side backend that reproduces the relevant backend behavior of the current `bartoostveen/ViTune` Android project: YouTube Music metadata/search/browse/playback discovery, lyrics, alternative Piped access, Kugou access, SponsorBlock, translation, caching, normalization, fallbacks, observability, and a stable API for clients.
4: >
5: > **Important accuracy rule:** This document distinguishes:
6: > - **VERIFIED FROM VITUNE SOURCE:** directly visible in the repository configuration/source available during this research.
7: > - **VERIFIED FROM LIVE CAPTURE:** directly visible in the user's uploaded YouTube Music `WEB_REMIX` response.
8: > - **VERIFIED FROM UPSTREAM DOCUMENTATION:** documented by the upstream service.
9: > - **IMPLEMENTATION RECOMMENDATION:** a backend design choice proposed here, not a claim that ViTune itself uses it.
10: >
11: > This is a compatibility-oriented engineering specification, not a claim that every internal implementation detail of ViTune can be reconstructed from public source alone.
12: 
13: ---
14: 
15: ## 1. Executive Summary
16: 
17: ViTune is structured as a provider-based Android music client. Its build configuration includes dedicated provider modules for:
18: 
19: ```text
20: providers:github
21: providers:innertube
22: providers:kugou
23: providers:lrclib
24: providers:piped
25: providers:sponsorblock
26: providers:translate
27: ```
28: 
29: and the app also bundles `yt-dlp` and `yt-dlp-ejs`.
30: 
31: The central architecture is therefore:
32: 
33: ```text
34:                               ┌────────────────────────┐
35:                               │      Your Backend      │
36:                               │                        │
37: Client ──────────────────────►│ API / Orchestrator     │
38:                               │                        │
39:                               │ Provider Router        │
40:                               └───────┬───────┬────────┘
41:                                       │       │
42:                  ┌────────────────────┘       └───────────────────┐
43:                  │                                                │
44:                  ▼                                                ▼
45:        ┌─────────────────┐                               ┌─────────────────┐
46:        │   InnerTube     │                               │     Lyrics      │
47:        │ YouTube Music   │                               │     LRCLIB      │
48:        └────────┬────────┘                               └─────────────────┘
49:                 │
50:        ┌────────┴────────┐
51:        │                 │
52:        ▼                 ▼
53:   YouTube metadata     Playback
54:                        discovery / extraction
55:                        via YouTube/yt-dlp/Piped
56: 
57:                  Additional providers:
58:                  ┌───────────────┐
59:                  │    Piped      │
60:                  ├───────────────┤
61:                  │    Kugou      │
62:                  ├───────────────┤
63:                  │ SponsorBlock  │
64:                  ├───────────────┤
65:                  │   Translate   │
66:                  └───────────────┘
67: ```
68: 
69: The key design principle is **normalize upstream-specific JSON into a stable internal schema** and expose only your stable schema to clients.
70: 
71: ---
72: 
73: # 2. Source Evidence and What Is Confirmed
74: 
75: ## 2.1 ViTune project structure
76:

78: 
79: ```text
80: :providers:common

82: :providers:innertube

85: :providers:piped

89:

93: 
94: ```text
95: yt-dlp>=2026.07.04
96: yt-dlp-ejs>=0.8.0
97: ```
98: 
99: through Chaquopy.
100: 
101: This confirms that ViTune has a distinct extraction/playback layer in addition to its metadata provider.
102: 
103: ---
104:

160: ---
161: 
162: # 3. Goals
163: 
164: The backend should support:
165: 
166: 1. Search.
167: 2. Song metadata.
168: 3. Artist metadata.
169: 4. Album metadata.
170: 5. Playlist metadata.
171: 6. YouTube Music browse pages.
172: 7. Continuation/pagination.
173: 8. Playback/stream resolution.
174: 9. Lyrics:
175:    - plain
176:    - line-synced
177: 10. Sponsor segment lookup.
178: 11. Optional alternative Piped playback.
179: 12. Optional Kugou metadata/lyrics fallback.
180: 13. Translation.
181: 14. Thumbnail proxying/normalization if desired.
182: 15. Provider health and failover.
183: 16. Response caching.
184: 17. Rate limiting.
185: 18. Request tracing.
186: 19. Stable normalized API independent of upstream renderer changes.
187: 
188: Non-goals:
189: 
190: - Do not reproduce every Android UI behavior.
191: - Do not expose raw upstream JSON as the primary public API.
192: - Do not store or redistribute copyrighted audio.
193: - Do not treat undocumented upstream interfaces as permanent contracts.
194: 
195: ---
196: 
197: # 4. Recommended Backend Technology
198: 
199: A practical implementation:
200: 
201: ```text
202: Language:       TypeScript
203: Runtime:        Node.js 22+
204: Framework:      Fastify
205: HTTP Client:    undici / native fetch
206: Validation:     Zod
207: Cache:          Redis
208: Primary DB:     PostgreSQL
209: Queue:          BullMQ or equivalent
210: Observability:  OpenTelemetry
211: Metrics:        Prometheus
212: Logs:           pino
213: Container:      Docker
214: Reverse Proxy:  Caddy / Nginx / Traefik
215: ```
216: 
217: A Rust implementation is also appropriate if very high concurrency and low overhead are priorities.
218: 
219: ---
220: 
221: # 5. System Architecture
222: 
223: ## 5.1 Layers
224: 
225: ```text
226: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
227: │                  HTTP API                   │
228: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
229: │          Authentication / Rate Limit        │
230: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
231: │              Application Layer              │
232: │ SearchService / TrackService / Lyrics...    │
233: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
234: │               Provider Router               │
235: ├──────────────┬──────────────┬───────────────┤
236: │ InnerTube    │ Piped        │ Kugou         │
237: │ LRCLIB       │ SponsorBlock │ Translate     │
238: ├──────────────┴──────────────┴───────────────┤
239: │          HTTP / JSON / Retry Layer          │
240: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
241: │ Redis / PostgreSQL / Metrics / Tracing      │
242: └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
243: ```
244: 
245: ## 5.2 Provider abstraction
246: 
247: Define one interface per capability rather than one giant interface.
248: 
249: ```ts
250: export interface SearchProvider {
251:   search(query: string, options?: SearchOptions): Promise<SearchResultPage>;
252: }
253: 
254: export interface TrackProvider {
255:   getTrack(id: string, options?: TrackOptions): Promise<Track>;
256: }
257: 
258: export interface ArtistProvider {
259:   getArtist(id: string): Promise<Artist>;
260: }
261: 
262: export interface AlbumProvider {
263:   getAlbum(id: string): Promise<Album>;
264: }
265: 
266: export interface PlaylistProvider {
267:   getPlaylist(id: string, continuation?: string): Promise<PlaylistPage>;
268: }
269: 
270: export interface StreamProvider {
271:   resolveStream(id: string, options?: StreamOptions): Promise<PlaybackInfo>;
272: }
273: 
274: export interface LyricsProvider {
275:   getLyrics(query: LyricsQuery): Promise<Lyrics | null>;
276: }
277: 
278: export interface SegmentProvider {
279:   getSegments(videoId: string): Promise<SponsorSegments>;
280: }
281: 
282: export interface TranslationProvider {
283:   translate(text: string, targetLanguage: string): Promise<string>;
284: }
285: ```
286:

303: ---
304: 
305: # 7. YouTube Music / InnerTube
306: 
307: ## 7.1 Base URL
308: 
309: The core endpoint family is:
310: 
311: ```text
312: https://music.youtube.com/youtubei/v1/
313: ```
314: 
315: For direct metadata/search calls, use the endpoint under that path.
316: 
317: Primary operations:
318: 
319: ```text
320: POST /youtubei/v1/search
321: POST /youtubei/v1/browse
322: POST /youtubei/v1/player
323: POST /youtubei/v1/next
324: ```
325: 
326: In practice, append:
327: 
328: ```text
329: ?prettyPrint=false
330: ```
331: 
332: for compact responses.
333: 
334: Example:
335: 
336: ```text
337: https://music.youtube.com/youtubei/v1/search?prettyPrint=false
338: ```
339: 
340: ---
341: 
342: # 8. InnerTube Request Headers
343: 
344: A minimal working unauthenticated search request is:
345: 
346: ```http
347: POST /youtubei/v1/search?prettyPrint=false HTTP/2
348: Host: music.youtube.com
349: Content-Type: application/json
350: User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0
351: Origin: https://music.youtube.com
352: Referer: https://music.youtube.com/
353: ```
354: 
355: Recommended production headers:
356: 
357: ```http
358: Content-Type: application/json
359: Accept: */*
360: Accept-Language: en-US,en;q=0.9
361: Origin: https://music.youtube.com
362: Referer: https://music.youtube.com/
363: User-Agent: <current browser-like UA>
364: ```
365: 
366: Depending on the chosen client and request type, additional YouTube-specific headers may be required:
367: 
368: ```text
369: x-youtube-client-name
370: x-youtube-client-version
371: x-goog-api-key
372: x-youtube-utc-offset
373: x-youtube-bootstrap-logged-in
374: ```
375: 
376: **Do not hard-code these unless the exact upstream client configuration requires them.**
377: 
378: ---

477:   .musicResponsiveListItemFlexColumnRenderer
478:   .text
479:   .runs[]
480:   .text
481: ```
482: 
483: The type and duration are commonly under the second flex column.
484: 
485: The raw result can expose:
486: 
487: ```text
488: title
489: duration
490: play count
491: videoId
492: thumbnail
493: album browseId
494: artist browseId
495: track credits browseId
496: musicVideoType
497: ```
498: 
499: ---
500: 
501: # 11. Canonical Internal Song Schema
502: 
503: Do not expose YouTube renderers publicly.
504: 
505: Use:
506: 
507: ```ts
508: export interface Song {
509:   id: string;                 // YouTube videoId or provider-native ID
510:   provider: "youtube" | "piped" | "kugou";
511:   title: string;
512:   subtitle?: string;
513:   artists: ArtistRef[];
514:   album?: AlbumRef;
515:   durationMs?: number;
516:   thumbnails: Thumbnail[];
517:   explicit?: boolean;
518:   isVideo?: boolean;
519:   musicVideoType?: string;
520:   playCount?: number;
521:   url?: string;
522:   source?: SourceRef;
523: }
524: ```
525: 
526: Artist:
527: 
528: ```ts
529: export interface ArtistRef {
530:   id?: string;
531:   name: string;
532: }
533: ```
534: 
535: Album:
536: 
537: ```ts
538: export interface AlbumRef {
539:   id?: string;
540:   name: string;
541: }
542: ```
543: 
544: Thumbnail:
545: 
546: ```ts
547: export interface Thumbnail {
548:   url: string;
549:   width: number;
550:   height: number;
551: }
552: ```
553: 
554: ---
555: 
556: # 12. Search API Exposed By Your Backend
557: 
558: Recommended endpoint:
559: 
560: ```http
561: GET /v1/search?q=Daft%20Punk&type=song&page=1
562: ```
563: 
564: Response:
565: 
566: ```json
567: {
568:   "items": [
569:     {
570:       "id": "khnokW3Mw24",
571:       "provider": "youtube",
572:       "title": "Instant Crush (feat. Julian Casablancas)",
573:       "artists": [
574:         {
575:           "id": "UCRr1xG_2WIDs18a6cIiCxeA",
576:           "name": "Daft Punk"
577:         }
578:       ],
579:       "album": {
580:         "id": "MPREb_K8qWMWVqXGi"
581:       },
582:       "durationMs": 338000,
583:       "thumbnails": [
584:         {
585:           "url": "https://...",
586:           "width": 120,
587:           "height": 120
588:         }
589:       ]
590:     }
591:   ],
592:   "continuation": null,
593:   "provider": "innertube"
594: }
595: ```
596: 
597: Recommended public query parameters:
598: 
599: ```text
600: q
601: type=song|album|artist|playlist|video
602: page
603: continuation
604: limit
605: region
606: language
607: ```
608: 
609: ---
610: 
611: # 13. Search Pagination / Continuations
612: 
613: InnerTube responses can contain continuation objects.
614: 
615: Never assume:
616: 
617: ```text
618: one request = complete result set
619: ```
620: 
621: Implement:
622: 
623: ```ts
624: interface SearchResultPage {
625:   items: Song[];
626:   continuation?: string;
627: }
628: ```
629: 
630: The public API should let the client send the opaque continuation token back:
631: 
632: ```http
633: GET /v1/search?q=Daft%20Punk&continuation=<opaque>
634: ```
635: 
636: Do not reinterpret an upstream continuation token.
637: 
638: Store no assumptions about its internal encoding.
639: 
640: ---
641: 
642: # 14. Browse
643: 
644: Browse is used to load entities and pages such as:
645: 
646: ```text
647: artist
648: album
649: playlist
650: charts
651: music pages
652: track credits
653: ```
654: 
655: Endpoint:
656: 
657: ```text
658: POST https://music.youtube.com/youtubei/v1/browse?prettyPrint=false
659: ```
660: 
661: The request uses:
662: 
663: ```json
664: {
665:   "context": {
666:     "client": {
667:       "clientName": "WEB_REMIX",
668:       "clientVersion": "1.20260821.01.00",
669:       "hl": "en",
670:       "gl": "US"
671:     }
672:   },
673:   "browseId": "<browseId>"
674: }
675: ```
676: 
677: Example artist browse ID observed in the live search result:
678: 
679: ```text
680: UCRr1xG_2WIDs18a6cIiCxeA
681: ```
682: 
683: Example album browse ID:
684: 
685: ```text
686: MPREb_K8qWMWVqXGi
687: ```
688: 
689: Track credits browse ID follows the observed pattern:
690: 
691: ```text
692: MPTC<videoId>
693: ```
694: 
695: Do not construct browse IDs manually if the upstream response already provides them. Treat the browse ID as opaque.
696: 
697: ---
698: 
699: # 15. Player
700: 
701: The player endpoint is:
702: 
703: ```text
704: POST https://music.youtube.com/youtubei/v1/player?prettyPrint=false
705: ```
706: 
707: Purpose:
708: 
709: ```text
710: videoId
711:   ↓
712: player
713:   ↓
714: playability status
715: metadata
716: streamingData
717: formats
718: adaptiveFormats
719: ```
720: 
721: Canonical request concept:
722: 
723: ```json
724: {
725:   "context": {
726:     "client": {
727:       "clientName": "WEB_REMIX",
728:       "clientVersion": "1.20260821.01.00",
729:       "hl": "en",
730:       "gl": "US"
731:     }
732:   },
733:   "videoId": "khnokW3Mw24"
734: }
735: ```
736: 
737: Possible raw response areas:
738: 
739: ```text
740: playabilityStatus
741: videoDetails
742: microformat
743: streamingData
744:   ├── formats[]
745:   └── adaptiveFormats[]
746: playerConfig
747: storyboards
748: ```
749: 
750: Important fields in a stream object can include:
751: 
752: ```text
753: itag
754: mimeType
755: bitrate
756: width
757: height
758: lastModified
759: contentLength
760: quality
761: qualityLabel
762: projectionType
763: averageBitrate
764: audioQuality
765: approxDurationMs
766: url
767: signatureCipher
768: cipher
769: ```
770: 
771: **Do not assume a direct `url` will always be present.**
772: 
773: Some streams can require deciphering and/or additional player logic.
774: 
775: ---
776: 
777: # 16. Playback Backend Strategy
778: 
779: Use a dedicated playback resolver:
780: 
781: ```text
782: resolvePlayback(videoId)
783:        │
784:        ├── InnerTube player
785:        │
786:        ├── Piped /streams/:videoId
787:        │
788:        └── yt-dlp / equivalent extractor
789: ```
790: 
791: Recommended preference:
792: 
793: ```text
794: 1. Cached still-valid playback URL
795: 2. Primary InnerTube player
796: 3. Piped
797: 4. yt-dlp
798: 5. Return structured failure
799: ```
800: 
801: Each candidate should be health-checked before being exposed to the client.
802: 
803: ---
804: 
805: # 17. Piped
806: 
807: Piped officially documents a public API with an instance-specific base URL.
808: 
809: Example documented instance:
810: 
811: ```text
812: https://pipedapi.kavin.rocks
813: ```
814: 
815: Piped explicitly warns that the instance list should be dynamically discovered instead of permanently assuming a single instance.
816: 
817: Documentation:
818: 
819: ```text
820: https://docs.piped.video/docs/api-documentation/
821: ```
822: 
823: ## 17.1 Streams
824: 
825: Endpoint:
826: 
827: ```text
828: GET /streams/:videoId
829: ```
830: 
831: Full example:
832: 
833: ```text
834: https://pipedapi.kavin.rocks/streams/khnokW3Mw24
835: ```
836: 
837: The documented response contains:
838: 
839: ```json
840: {
841:   "audioStreams": [
842:     {
843:       "bitrate": 0,
844:       "codec": "...",
845:       "format": "...",
846:       "mimeType": "audio/mp4",
847:       "quality": "...",
848:       "url": "https://...",
849:       "itag": 0
850:     }
851:   ],
852:   "videoStreams": [
853:     {
854:       "bitrate": 0,
855:       "codec": "avc1.64002a",
856:       "format": "MPEG_4",
857:       "fps": 30,
858:       "height": 720,
859:       "indexEnd": 0,
860:       "indexStart": 0,
861:       "initStart": 0,
862:       "initEnd": 0,
863:       "mimeType": "video/mp4",
864:       "quality": "720p",
865:       "url": "https://...",
866:       "videoOnly": false,
867:       "width": 1280
868:     }
869:   ],
870:   "views": 0
871: }
872: ```
873: 
874: Piped's API documentation also exposes channel and other metadata endpoints.
875: 
876: ---
877: 
878: # 18. Piped Base URL Selection
879: 
880: Do not hard-code one public Piped instance in production.
881: 
882: Create:
883: 
884: ```ts
885: interface PipedInstance {
886:   apiBase: string;
887:   proxyBase?: string;
888:   healthy: boolean;
889:   latencyMs?: number;
890: }
891: ```
892: 
893: Discover instances from:
894: 
895: ```text
896: https://github.com/TeamPiped/Piped/wiki/Instances
897: ```
898: 
899: At startup and periodically:
900: 
901: ```text
902: discover instances
903:       ↓
904: probe /streams/<known-video-id>
905:       ↓
906: record:
907:   status
908:   latency
909:   TLS validity
910:   response correctness
911:       ↓
912: rank healthy instances
913: ```
914: 
915: ---
916: 
917: # 19. LRCLIB
918: 
919: The project's provider list confirms a dedicated LRCLIB provider.
920: 
921: The documented API base is:
922: 
923: ```text
924: https://lrclib.net/api
925: ```
926: 
927: The documented endpoints include:
928: 
929: ```text
930: GET  /api/get
931: GET  /api/get/{id}
932: GET  /api/search
933: GET  /api/get-cached
934: POST /api/request-challenge
935: POST /api/publish
936: POST /api/flag
937: ```
938: 
939: For a playback client, the two primary read operations are:
940: 
941: ```text
942: GET /api/get
943: GET /api/search
944: ```
945: 
946: ## 19.1 Exact metadata lookup
947: 
948: Conceptual request:
949: 
950: ```text
951: GET https://lrclib.net/api/get
952:   ?track_name=Instant%20Crush
953:   &artist_name=Daft%20Punk
954:   &album_name=Random%20Access%20Memories
955:   &duration=338
956: ```
957: 
958: The metadata lookup should use:
959: 
960: ```text
961: track_name
962: artist_name
963: album_name
964: duration
965: ```
966: 
967: where available.
968: 
969: ## 19.2 Search
970: 
971: ```text
972: GET https://lrclib.net/api/search?q=Daft%20Punk
973: ```
974: 
975: or the query fields supported by the current LRCLIB API version.
976: 
977: Canonical normalized model:
978: 
979: ```ts
980: interface Lyrics {
981:   trackId?: number;
982:   trackName: string;
983:   artistName: string;
984:   albumName?: string;
985:   duration?: number;
986:   plainLyrics?: string | null;
987:   syncedLyrics?: string | null;
988: }
989: ```
990: 
991: Do not publish lyrics data without considering the upstream service/license conditions.
992: 
993: ---
994: 
995: # 20. Lyrics Matching Algorithm
996: 
997: Recommended order:
998: 
999: ```text
1000: 1. Exact title + exact artist + exact duration
1001: 2. Exact title + artist + approximate duration
1002: 3. Search title + artist
1003: 4. Search normalized title + normalized artist
1004: ```
1005: 
1006: Normalize:
1007: 
1008: ```text
1009: case
1010: Unicode punctuation
1011: feat./ft./featuring
1012: parentheses
1013: hyphens
1014: extra whitespace
1015: ```
1016: 
1017: Duration match:
1018: 
1019: ```text
1020: abs(candidateDuration - trackDuration) <= 3 seconds
1021: ```
1022: 
1023: Use a larger tolerance only as a fallback.
1024:

1026: 
1027: # 21. Kugou
1028: 
1029: The project contains a dedicated Kugou provider.
1030: 
1031: Public third-party documentation shows a song search endpoint:
1032: 
1033: ```text
1034: http://msearchcdn.kugou.com/api/v3/search/song
1035: ```
1036: 
1037: Required parameters documented by one API reference:
1038: 
1039: ```text
1040: plat=0
1041: keyword=<query>
1042: version=9108
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: Useful optional parameters:
1046: 
1047: ```text
1048: pagesize
1049: page
1050: highlight
1051: tagtype
1052: tag_aggr
1053: ```
1054: 
1055: Example:
1056: 
1057: ```text
1058: http://msearchcdn.kugou.com/api/v3/search/song?plat=0&keyword=Daft%20Punk&pagesize=20&version=9108
1059: ```
1060: 
1061: Other historically documented Kugou endpoints include:
1062: 
1063: ```text
1064: http://mobilecdn.kugou.com/api/v3/search/song
1065: http://mobilecdn.kugou.com/api/v3/search/special
1066: http://msearch.kugou.com/api/v3/search/mv
1067: http://msearch.kugou.com/api/v3/search/album
1068: http://mobileservice.kugou.com/api/v3/lyric/search
1069: ```
1070: 
1071: **Caution:** Kugou endpoint documentation available publicly is often reverse-engineered and version-dependent. Treat these as adapter endpoints and expect breakage.
1072: 
1073: ---
1074: 
1075: # 22. Kugou Response Shape
1076: 
1077: A commonly documented search response is structurally:
1078: 
1079: ```json
1080: {
1081:   "status": 1,
1082:   "error": "",
1083:   "data": {
1084:     "aggregation": [],
1085:     "timestamp": 0,
1086:     "info": [
1087:       {
1088:         "songname": "...",
1089:         "singername": "...",
1090:         "album_name": "...",
1091:         "hash": "...",
1092:         "duration": 0,
1093:         "album_id": 0,
1094:         "singerid": 0,
1095:         "trans_param": {}
1096:       }
1097:     ]
1098:   },
1099:   "errcode": 0
1100: }
1101: ```
1102: 
1103: Because Kugou's response fields vary by endpoint/version, the adapter should parse defensively.
1104:

1106: 
1107: # 23. SponsorBlock
1108: 
1109: SponsorBlock is a separate crowd-sourced segment service.
1110: 
1111: Documented public API:
1112: 
1113: ```text
1114: https://sponsor.ajay.app
1115: ```
1116: 
1117: API documentation:
1118: 
1119: ```text
1120: https://github.com/ajayyy/SponsorBlock/wiki/API-Docs
1121: ```
1122: 
1123: A relevant operation is retrieving segments associated with a video.
1124: 
1125: Conceptual request:
1126: 
1127: ```text
1128: GET https://sponsor.ajay.app/api/skipSegments/<hash>
1129: ```
1130: 
1131: or the current API-equivalent query documented by SponsorBlock.
1132: 
1133: The response contains segment objects with fields such as:
1134: 
1135: ```json
1136: {
1137:   "segment": [0, 10],
1138:   "category": "sponsor",
1139:   "actionType": "skip",
1140:   "videoDuration": 0,
1141:   "UUID": "..."
1142: }
1143: ```
1144: 
1145: Do not hard-code the precise path from old third-party examples; verify against the current SponsorBlock API documentation at implementation time.
1146: 
1147: ---
1148: 
1149: # 24. SponsorBlock Normalized Schema
1150: 
1151: ```ts
1152: interface SponsorSegment {
1153:   id: string;
1154:   startMs: number;
1155:   endMs: number;
1156:   category:
1157:     | "sponsor"
1158:     | "intro"
1159:     | "outro"
1160:     | "selfpromo"
1161:     | "interaction"
1162:     | "music_offtopic"
1163:     | "preview"
1164:     | "filler"
1165:     | string;
1166:   action: "skip" | string;
1167: }
1168: ```
1169: 
1170: ---
1171: 
1172: # 25. Translation Provider
1173: 
1174: The repository contains:
1175: 
1176: ```text
1177: providers:translate
1178: ```
1179: 
1180: but the publicly surfaced repository configuration does not expose enough evidence here to assert a single exact external translation endpoint.
1181: 
1182: Therefore:
1183: 
1184: **Do not claim an exact Google Translate/LibreTranslate/etc. URL for ViTune without inspecting the provider source itself.**
1185: 
1186: For your backend, use an abstraction:
1187: 
1188: ```ts
1189: interface TranslationProvider {
1190:   translate(
1191:     text: string,
1192:     sourceLanguage: string | undefined,
1193:     targetLanguage: string
1194:   ): Promise<{
1195:     text: string;
1196:     sourceLanguage?: string;
1197:     targetLanguage: string;
1198:   }>;
1199: }
1200: ```
1201: 
1202: Implementation options:
1203: 
1204: ```text
1205: LibreTranslate
1206: Google Cloud Translation
1207: DeepL
1208: self-hosted NLLB/Marian
1209: ```
1210: 
1211: Choose one explicitly rather than assuming the ViTune provider implementation.
1212: 
1213: ---
1214: 
1215: # 26. GitHub Provider
1216: 
1217: The repository also contains:
1218: 
1219: ```text
1220: providers:github
1221: ```
1222: 
1223: but the available evidence does not justify claiming a specific GitHub endpoint or runtime dependency for music metadata.
1224: 
1225: Treat GitHub integration as a separate provider capability.
1226: 
1227: If your backend needs release metadata:
1228: 
1229: ```text
1230: GET https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>/releases/latest
1231: ```
1232: 
1233: is an example of the public GitHub API, but this is an implementation choice, not a verified ViTune runtime contract.

1373: # 32. `/v1/lyrics`
1374: 
1375: Request:
1376: 
1377: ```http
1378: GET /v1/lyrics?title=Instant%20Crush&artist=Daft%20Punk&album=Random%20Access%20Memories&duration=338
1379: ```
1380: 
1381: Response:
1382: 
1383: ```json
1384: {
1385:   "found": true,
1386:   "source": "lrclib",
1387:   "track": {
1388:     "title": "Instant Crush",
1389:     "artist": "Daft Punk",
1390:     "album": "Random Access Memories"
1391:   },
1392:   "durationMs": 338000,
1393:   "plainLyrics": "...",
1394:   "syncedLyrics": "[00:12.00]..."
1395: }
1396: ```
1397: 
1398: No-found response:
1399: 
1400: ```json
1401: {
1402:   "found": false,
1403:   "source": null,
1404:   "track": {
1405:     "title": "Unknown",
1406:     "artist": "Unknown"
1407:   },
1408:   "plainLyrics": null,
1409:   "syncedLyrics": null
1410: }
1411: ```
1412: 
1413: ---
1414: 
1415: # 33. `/v1/streams/:id`
1416: 
1417: Use a provider-neutral stream schema.
1418: 
1419: ```json
1420: {
1421:   "id": "khnokW3Mw24",
1422:   "provider": "piped",
1423:   "expiresAt": "2026-08-22T18:00:00Z",
1424:   "audio": [
1425:     {
1426:       "url": "https://...",
1427:       "mimeType": "audio/mp4",
1428:       "codec": "mp4a.40.2",
1429:       "bitrate": 128000,
1430:       "sampleRate": 48000,
1431:       "channels": 2,
1432:       "contentLength": null
1433:     }
1434:   ],
1435:   "video": []
1436: }
1437: ```
1438: 
1439: Never assume a signed URL is permanent.
1440: 
1441: ---
1442: 
1443: # 34. URL Expiration and Playback Caching
1444: 
1445: Do not cache a stream URL for the same duration as metadata.
1446: 
1447: Use:
1448: 
1449: ```text
1450: metadata TTL: 6h–24h
1451: artist TTL: 6h–24h
1452: album TTL: 6h
1453: playlist TTL: 5m–1h
1454: search TTL: 30s–5m
1455: lyrics TTL: 7d
1456: stream URL TTL: short, provider-dependent
1457: ```
1458: 
1459: Prefer:
1460: 
1461: ```text
1462: Cache-Control / upstream expiry timestamp
1463: ```
1464: 
1465: over hard-coded stream lifetimes.
1466: 
1467: ---
1468: 
1469: # 35. Cache Keys
1470: 
1471: Recommended:
1472: 
1473: ```text
1474: yt:search:{region}:{language}:{normalizedQuery}:{type}:{continuationHash}
1475: 
1476: yt:song:{videoId}
1477: 
1478: yt:artist:{browseId}
1479: 
1480: yt:album:{browseId}
1481: 
1482: yt:playlist:{browseId}
1483: 
1484: stream:{videoId}:{clientProfile}
1485: 
1486: lyrics:{sha256(title|artist|album|duration)}
1487: 
1488: sponsor:{videoId}
1489: ```
1490: 
1491: ---
1492: 
1493: # 36. Cache Stampede Protection
1494: 
1495: For hot tracks:
1496: 
1497: ```text
1498: GET cache miss
1499:       ↓
1500: distributed lock
1501:       ↓
1502: one request fetches upstream
1503:       ↓
1504: other requests wait briefly
1505:       ↓
1506: result stored
1507: ```
1508: 
1509: Use Redis:
1510: 
1511: ```text
1512: SET lock:key value NX PX 5000
1513: ```
1514: 
1515: with a unique lock owner/token.
1516: 
1517: ---
1518: 
1519: # 37. Database
1520: 
1521: You do not need to persist every upstream object.
1522: 
1523: Recommended tables:
1524: 
1525: ```text
1526: songs
1527: artists
1528: albums
1529: playlists
1530: playlist_items
1531: song_aliases
1532: provider_ids
1533: lyrics_cache
1534: provider_health
1535: request_log
1536: ```
1537: 
1538: ## 37.1 songs
1539: 
1540: ```sql
1541: CREATE TABLE songs (
1542:   id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
1543:   canonical_provider TEXT NOT NULL,
1544:   provider_song_id TEXT NOT NULL,
1545:   title TEXT NOT NULL,
1546:   duration_ms INTEGER,
1547:   explicit BOOLEAN,
1548:   created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
1549:   updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
1550:   UNIQUE(canonical_provider, provider_song_id)
1551: );
1552: ```
1553: 
1554: ## 37.2 provider_ids
1555: 
1556: ```sql
1557: CREATE TABLE provider_ids (
1558:   song_id UUID NOT NULL,
1559:   provider TEXT NOT NULL,
1560:   provider_id TEXT NOT NULL,
1561:   metadata JSONB,
1562:   PRIMARY KEY(song_id, provider)
1563: );
1564: ```
1565: 
1566: This lets one canonical song map to:
1567: 
1568: ```text
1569: YouTube videoId
1570: Kugou hash
1571: Piped video ID
1572: other provider IDs
1573: ```
1574: 
1575: ---
1576: 
1577: # 38. Search Normalization
1578: 
1579: Input:
1580: 
1581: ```text
1582: "  Daft  Punk  "
1583: ```
1584: 
1585: Normalize to:
1586: 
1587: ```text
1588: "daft punk"
1589: ```
1590: 
1591: Rules:
1592: 
1593: ```text
1594: Unicode NFKC
1595: trim
1596: collapse whitespace
1597: lowercase for cache key
1598: preserve original query for upstream
1599: ```
1600: 
1601: Do not remove punctuation before sending upstream unless required.
1602: 
1603: ---
1604: 
1605: # 39. Metadata Merge
1606: 
1607: When multiple providers return the same track:
1608: 
1609: ```text
1610: YouTube:
1611:   title
1612:   duration
1613:   artist
1614:   album
1615: 
1616: Kugou:
1617:   hash
1618:   alternate lyrics metadata
1619: 
1620: LRCLIB:
1621:   lyrics
1622: 
1623: Piped:
1624:   playback
1625: 
1626: SponsorBlock:
1627:   segments
1628: ```
1629: 
1630: Do not overwrite values blindly.
1631: 
1632: Use field precedence:
1633: 
1634: ```text
1635: canonical title:
1636:   YouTube Music > Kugou
1637: 
1638: duration:
1639:   YouTube > Piped > Kugou
1640: 
1641: artist:
1642:   YouTube Music > Kugou
1643: 
1644: album:
1645:   YouTube Music > Kugou
1646: 
1647: lyrics:
1648:   LRCLIB > Kugou fallback
1649: 
1650: stream:
1651:   healthy primary resolver > fallback
1652: ```
1653: 
1654: ---
1655: 
1656: # 40. Provider Failure Taxonomy
1657: 
1658: Every provider error should map into:
1659: 
1660: ```ts
1661: type ProviderErrorCode =
1662:   | "TIMEOUT"
1663:   | "RATE_LIMITED"
1664:   | "UNAUTHORIZED"
1665:   | "FORBIDDEN"
1666:   | "NOT_FOUND"
1667:   | "UNPLAYABLE"
1668:   | "BAD_RESPONSE"
1669:   | "UPSTREAM_5XX"
1670:   | "UPSTREAM_4XX"
1671:   | "PARSER_ERROR"
1672:   | "INSTANCE_UNHEALTHY"
1673:   | "UNKNOWN";
1674: ```
1675: 
1676: Never leak raw upstream stack traces to clients.
1677: 
1678: ---
1679: 
1680: # 41. Retry Policy
1681: 
1682: Retry only safe/idempotent requests.
1683: 
1684: Recommended:
1685: 
1686: ```text
1687: Timeout:
1688:   250ms → 750ms → 1500ms
1689: 
1690: HTTP 429:
1691:   respect Retry-After
1692: 
1693: HTTP 5xx:
1694:   250ms → 750ms → 1500ms
1695: 
1696: HTTP 4xx:
1697:   generally no retry
1698: ```
1699: 
1700: Limit total upstream attempts:
1701: 
1702: ```text
1703: search: 2
1704: metadata: 2
1705: lyrics: 2
1706: playback: 3+
1707: ```
1708: 
1709: ---
1710: 
1711: # 42. Circuit Breakers
1712: 
1713: Maintain per-provider:
1714: 
1715: ```text
1716: state:
1717:   CLOSED
1718:   OPEN
1719:   HALF_OPEN
1720: ```
1721: 
1722: Trip when:
1723: 
1724: ```text
1725: 5xx rate > 30%
1726: or timeout rate > 30%
1727: or 5 consecutive failures
1728: ```
1729: 
1730: Reset after:
1731: 
1732: ```text
1733: 15–30 seconds
1734: ```
1735: 
1736: Tune using real production telemetry.
1737: 
1738: ---
1739: 
1740: # 43. Piped Instance Health
1741: 
1742: For each Piped instance record:
1743: 
1744: ```text
1745: instance URL
1746: last success
1747: last failure
1748: latency p50
1749: latency p95
1750: success rate
1751: TLS status
1752: last tested endpoint
1753: ```
1754: 
1755: Probe:
1756: 
1757: ```text
1758: /streams/<known-video-id>
1759: ```
1760: 
1761: If the instance has an unhealthy proxy domain, mark the instance degraded.
1762: 
1763: ---
1764: 
1765: # 44. Observability
1766: 
1767: Every request gets:
1768: 
1769: ```text
1770: request_id
1771: trace_id
1772: provider
1773: operation
1774: upstream_url
1775: status
1776: latency_ms
1777: retry_count
1778: cache_hit
1779: response_bytes
1780: ```
1781: 
1782: Metrics:
1783: 
1784: ```text
1785: http_requests_total
1786: http_request_duration_ms
1787: provider_requests_total
1788: provider_request_duration_ms
1789: provider_errors_total
1790: cache_hits_total
1791: cache_misses_total
1792: stream_resolution_success_total
1793: stream_resolution_failure_total
1794: lyrics_hits_total
1795: lyrics_misses_total
1796: ```
1797: 
1798: ---
1799: 
1800: # 45. OpenTelemetry
1801: 
1802: Create spans:
1803: 
1804: ```text
1805: HTTP GET /v1/search
1806: └── provider.search
1807:     └── http POST music.youtube.com/youtubei/v1/search
1808: ```
1809: 
1810: For playback:
1811: 
1812: ```text
1813: GET /v1/streams/:id
1814: └── stream.resolve
1815:     ├── cache.get
1816:     ├── innertube.player
1817:     ├── piped.streams
1818:     └── extractor.resolve
1819: ```
1820: 
1821: Do not record cookies, authorization tokens, or other secrets as span attributes.
1822: 
1823: ---
1824: 
1825: # 46. Security
1826: 
1827: ## Required
1828: 
1829: - TLS.
1830: - Request size limits.
1831: - Query length limits.
1832: - SSRF protection.
1833: - URL allowlisting for server-side fetches.
1834: - Rate limiting.
1835: - Redis authentication.
1836: - DB credentials via secrets.
1837: - No provider credentials in logs.
1838: - No user cookies in logs.
1839: 
1840: ## SSRF protection
1841: 
1842: Never allow clients to send arbitrary:
1843: 
1844: ```text
1845: url=https://anything
1846: ```
1847: 
1848: to a generic backend fetch endpoint.
1849: 
1850: Provider URLs must be constructed from allowlisted base URLs.
1851: 
1852: ---
1853: 
1854: # 47. Rate Limiting
1855: 
1856: Suggested initial limits:
1857: 
1858: ```text
1859: unauthenticated search:
1860:   30 requests/min/IP
1861: 
1862: metadata:
1863:   120 requests/min/IP
1864: 
1865: lyrics:
1866:   60 requests/min/IP
1867: 
1868: playback:
1869:   60 requests/min/IP
1870: ```
1871: 
1872: These are backend recommendations, not ViTune values.
1873: 
1874: Use Redis token bucket/sliding window.
1875: 
1876: ---
1877: 
1878: # 48. Concurrency Limits
1879: 
1880: Per provider:
1881: 
1882: ```text
1883: InnerTube: 20 concurrent
1884: Piped:     20 per instance
1885: Kugou:     10
1886: LRCLIB:    10
1887: SponsorBlock: 20
1888: Translate: 5
1889: ```
1890: 
1891: Tune based on provider response and rate limits.
1892: 
1893: ---
1894: 
1895: # 49. Provider Router
1896: 
1897: Example:
1898: 
1899: ```ts
1900: class ProviderRouter {
1901:   constructor(
1902:     private readonly innerTube: InnerTubeProvider,
1903:     private readonly piped: PipedProvider,
1904:     private readonly kugou: KugouProvider,
1905:     private readonly lrclib: LrclibProvider,
1906:     private readonly sponsorBlock: SponsorBlockProvider,
1907:     private readonly translate: TranslationProvider,
1908:   ) {}
1909: 
1910:   async search(query: string) {
1911:     try {
1912:       return await this.innerTube.search(query);
1913:     } catch {
1914:       try {
1915:         return await this.piped.search(query);
1916:       } catch {
1917:         return await this.kugou.search(query);
1918:       }
1919:     }
1920:   }
1921: }
1922: ```
1923: 
1924: Production implementation should add:
1925: 
1926: ```text
1927: timeouts
1928: metrics
1929: circuit breaker
1930: cache
1931: structured errors
1932: ```
1933: 
1934: ---
1935: 
1936: # 50. Search Fallback Strategy
1937: 
1938: Preferred:
1939: 
1940: ```text
1941: InnerTube
1942:     │
1943:     ├── success → return
1944:     │
1945:     └── fail
1946:           ↓
1947:         Piped
1948:           │
1949:           ├── success → return
1950:           │
1951:           └── fail
1952:                 ↓
1953:               Kugou
1954: ```
1955: 
1956: Do not merge unrelated result sets unless explicitly requested.
1957: 
1958: The default behavior should be:
1959: 
1960: ```text
1961: one canonical provider result set
1962: ```
1963: 
1964: with provider fallback only on error.
1965: 
1966: ---
1967: 
1968: # 51. Stream Fallback Strategy
1969: 
1970: ```text
1971: 1. InnerTube player
1972: 2. Piped /streams
1973: 3. yt-dlp
1974: 4. fail with structured error
1975: ```
1976: 
1977: For each resolver:
1978: 
1979: ```ts
1980: interface PlaybackResolver {
1981:   resolve(videoId: string): Promise<PlaybackInfo>;
1982: }
1983: ```
1984: 
1985: The final resolver should return the same normalized schema.
1986: 
1987: ---
1988: 
1989: # 52. `yt-dlp` Integration
1990: 
1991: ViTune's Android build configuration explicitly installs:
1992: 
1993: ```text
1994: yt-dlp>=2026.07.04
1995: yt-dlp-ejs>=0.8.0
1996: ```
1997: 
1998: For a backend implementation, isolate yt-dlp:
1999: 
2000: ```text
````

```text
233:             self.message
234:         )
235:     }
236: }

240: /// Capability traits — §5.2, one per capability, not one giant trait.
241: pub trait SearchProvider: Send + Sync {
242:     fn search(
243:         &self,
244:         query: &str,
245:         options: &SearchOptions,
246:     ) -> Result<SearchResultPage, ProviderError>;
247: }

251: }

255: }

259: }

261: /// Circuit breaker state — §42.
262: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
263: pub enum CircuitState {
264:     Closed,
265:     Open,
266:     HalfOpen,
267: }
268: 
269: #[derive(Debug)]
270: pub struct CircuitBreaker {
271:     state: std::sync::Mutex<CircuitInner>,
272:     failure_threshold: u32,
273:     reset_after: Duration,
274: }
275: 
276: #[derive(Debug)]
277: struct CircuitInner {
278:     state: CircuitState,
279:     consecutive_failures: u32,
280:     opened_at: Option<std::time::Instant>,
281: }
282: 
283: impl CircuitBreaker {
284:     pub fn new(failure_threshold: u32, reset_after: Duration) -> Self {
285:         Self {
286:             state: std::sync::Mutex::new(CircuitInner {
287:                 state: CircuitState::Closed,
288:                 consecutive_failures: 0,
289:                 opened_at: None,
290:             }),
291:             failure_threshold,
292:             reset_after,
293:         }
294:     }
295: 
296:     pub fn allow_request(&self) -> bool {
297:         let mut inner = self.state.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
298:         match inner.state {
299:             CircuitState::Closed => true,
300:             CircuitState::Open => {
301:                 if inner
302:                     .opened_at
303:                     .is_some_and(|t| t.elapsed() >= self.reset_after)
304:                 {
305:                     inner.state = CircuitState::HalfOpen;
306:                     true
307:                 } else {
308:                     false
309:                 }
310:             }
311:             CircuitState::HalfOpen => true,
312:         }
313:     }
314: 
315:     pub fn record_success(&self) {
316:         let mut inner = self.state.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
317:         inner.consecutive_failures = 0;
318:         inner.state = CircuitState::Closed;
319:         inner.opened_at = None;
320:     }
321: 
322:     pub fn record_failure(&self) {
323:         let mut inner = self.state.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
324:         inner.consecutive_failures += 1;
325:         if inner.consecutive_failures >= self.failure_threshold {
326:             inner.state = CircuitState::Open;
327:             inner.opened_at = Some(std::time::Instant::now());
328:         }
329:     }
330: 
331:     pub fn state(&self) -> CircuitState {
332:         self.state.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner()).state
333:     }
334: }
335:

355:         assert_eq!(cb.state(), CircuitState::Closed);
356:         cb.record_failure();

358:         assert_eq!(cb.state(), CircuitState::Closed);
359:         cb.record_failure();
360:         assert_eq!(cb.state(), CircuitState::Open);
361:         assert!(!cb.allow_request());
362:         cb.record_success();
363:         assert_eq!(cb.state(), CircuitState::Closed);
364:         assert!(cb.allow_request());
```

```text
325: fn video_from(v: &serde_json::Value) -> Option<YtVideo> {
326:     let id = v["id"].as_str()?;
327:     let title = v["title"].as_str().unwrap_or("").to_string();
328:     let artist = v["artist"]
329:         .as_str()
330:         .or_else(|| v["channel"].as_str())
331:         .or_else(|| v["uploader"].as_str())

338:         // (u64::MAX × 1000 overflows before the u32 try_from can guard it).
339:         .and_then(|s| s.checked_mul(1000))
340:         .and_then(|ms| u32::try_from(ms).ok());

364: /// Wait up to `deadline` for one of `p`'s permits, polling every 50ms.
365: /// `None` means the budget is exhausted: the caller MUST fail open (spawn
366: /// anyway and block for a permit) — a permit-shaped `None` must never surface
367: /// as a request failure, because `yt_stdout`'s `None` is a dropped stream to
368: /// the engine. In production `None` only appears under pathological
369: /// contention, where the fail-open fallback blocks until a permit frees
370: /// (unbounded wait; the single-permit cap is retained).
371: fn wait_for_permit(p: &Semaphore, deadline: Instant) -> Option<SemaphorePermit<'_>> {
372:     loop {
373:         if let Ok(permit) = p.try_acquire() {
374:             return Some(permit);
375:         }
376:         if Instant::now() >= deadline {
377:             return None;
378:         }
379:         std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50));
380:     }
381: }

383: /// Run `yt-dlp … -J` and parse its dumped JSON.
384: fn yt_json(extra: &[&str], cancel: Option<Arc<AtomicBool>>) -> Option<serde_json::Value> {
385:     yt_stdout(&["-J"], extra, cancel).and_then(|s| serde_json::from_str(&s).ok())
386: }

388: /// The stream leg is resolved with the `android` player client. On this box
389: /// (verified 2026-08-16, bead Myx-jqp) URLs from the default/web/tv clients
390: /// stall at the transport level — ffmpeg connects and receives 0 bytes in
391: /// 15 s, while the `android` client's URL flows instantly (~180 ms to first
392: /// PCM, 3/3 runs vs 0/9 for the others). A stalled URL starves the engine's
393: /// prebuffer → silent playback, ALSA underrun errors, frozen position and
394: /// visualizer, and watchdog rebuild loops.
395: ///
396: /// Trade-off: the android client exposes no audio-only itags — `-f bestaudio`
397: /// hard-fails under it, so the `/best` fallback below always lands on the
398: /// muxed (360p video + audio) stream, wasting bandwidth the engine never
399: /// decodes. That cost is deliberate: an unthrottled stream is worth 3× the
400: /// bytes; a user-set `audio_format` without a fallback is tolerated by
401: /// appending `/best` rather than letting resolution fail.
402: const STREAM_PLAYER_CLIENT: &str = "android";
403: 
404: /// Pull the direct stream URL out of a `-J` info dump — the same pick the old
405: /// `-g -f <configured>/best` leg made, now from the dump's own data:
406: /// 1. a `formats[]` entry whose `format_id` equals a bare `configured` (a
407: ///    user's `audio_format = "251"` must select that exact itag);
408: /// 2. otherwise the *last playable* entry — the android dump appends
409: ///    storyboard entries (`sb*`, both codecs "none") after the real stream,
410: ///    so the naive "last entry" would hand back a storyboard URL;
411: /// 3. finally the info dict's own top-level `url` — which with `-f` active is
412: ///    exactly the format `-g` would have printed.
413: fn pick_url<'a>(root: &'a serde_json::Value, configured: &str) -> Option<&'a str> {
414:     if let Some(entries) = root["formats"].as_array() {
415:         if !configured.contains('/') {
416:             if let Some(f) = entries
417:                 .iter()
418:                 .find(|f| f["format_id"].as_str() == Some(configured))
419:                 .and_then(|f| f["url"].as_str())
420:             {
421:                 return Some(f);
422:             }
423:         }
424:         if let Some(f) = entries.iter().rev().find(|f| {
425:             let playable = f["vcodec"].as_str().is_some_and(|v| v != "none")
426:                 || f["acodec"].as_str().is_some_and(|a| a != "none");
427:             playable && f["url"].as_str().is_some()
428:         }) {
429:             return f["url"].as_str();
430:         }
431:     }
432:     root["url"].as_str()
433: }

435: /// Run the configured yt-dlp binary with `base + extra` args and capture
436: /// stdout; `None` on launch failure, non-zero exit, or invalid UTF-8. Errors
437: /// are logged, not propagated — the api layer's Option/empty convention.
438: ///
439: /// Two bounds keep a yt-dlp child from ever wedging a worker thread:
440: /// `--retries 1` cuts yt-dlp's own default retry chain (which can sleep for
441: /// minutes on a 429), and the child is killed outright once it outlives
442: /// `SOCKET_TIMEOUT_SECS` + a small margin (a stalled socket must not hold a
443: /// blocking thread hostage while the app's own deadline has given up on it).
444: ///
445: /// The pipes MUST be drained while the child runs: a `-J` dump is ~600 KB and
446: /// yt-dlp blocks on a full 64 KB pipe unless something reads it, so a plain
447: /// poll-and-kill loop would deadlock until the deadline kills the child.
448: /// Reader threads therefore own the drains; the caller thread owns the child
449: /// (for `try_wait`/`kill`, which need `&mut`) and joins the readers once the
450: /// process is gone. Killing guarantees EOF on both pipes, so the joins always
451: /// return.
452: fn yt_stdout(base: &[&str], extra: &[&str], cancel: Option<Arc<AtomicBool>>) -> Option<String> {
453:     let bin = config::get().ytdlp_path.clone();
454:     yt_stdout_with_bin(&bin, base, extra, cancel)
455: }
456: 
457: /// The [`yt_stdout`] core with the binary injected — the config read stays at
458: /// the public boundary so tests can point the seam at a fake binary and run
459: /// the cancellability (F13) and concurrency-cap (F17) paths fully offline.
460: fn yt_stdout_with_bin(
461:     bin: &str,
462:     base: &[&str],
463:     extra: &[&str],
464:     cancel: Option<Arc<AtomicBool>>,
465: ) -> Option<String> {
466:     // F17: the RAII permit is held across the child's WHOLE life — spawn
467:     // through both drain joins — and drops on every early-return path below.
468:     // The bounded wait shares the child's own deadline; on budget exhaustion
469:     // the wait fails OPEN immediately (run unpermitted, log it) — an
470:     // unbounded blocking acquire here would hold the engine worker past its
471:     // resolve deadline, so the cap degrades to today's concurrency instead of
472:     // manufacturing a hang (audit F17 regression caution).
473:     let deadline =
474:         Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs((SOCKET_TIMEOUT_SECS + DEADLINE_MARGIN_SECS) as u64);
475:     let _permit = match wait_for_permit(&YTDLP_PERMIT, deadline) {
476:         Some(permit) => Some(permit),
477:         None => {
478:             liblog("yt: yt-dlp budget exhausted — running unpermitted (fail-open)");
479:             None
480:         }
481:     };
482:     let mut child = std::process::Command::new(bin)
483:         .args([
484:             "--no-warnings",
485:             "--socket-timeout",
486:             &SOCKET_TIMEOUT_SECS.to_string(),
487:             "--retries",
488:             "1",
489:         ])
490:         .args(base)
491:         // A TUI's stdin must never leak into the CLI child: with tuna-tui run under a
492:         // pipe (tests, streaming, probes) yt-dlp can stall on an inherited,
493:         // never-EOF stdin instead of doing its job. ffmpeg gets the same
494:         // treatment (`spawn_ffmpeg`).
495:         .stdin(std::process::Stdio::null())
496:         .args(extra)
497:         // Optional session cookies (`--cookies`): without them private
498:         // playlists / history are inaccessible and traffic is bot-checked.
499:         .args(match &config::get().cookies_file {
500:             Some(path) => vec!["--cookies", path.as_str()],
501:             None => vec![],
502:         })
503:         .stdout(std::process::Stdio::piped())
504:         .stderr(std::process::Stdio::piped())
505:         .spawn()
506:         .ok()?;
507:     let mut stdout = child.stdout.take();
508:     let mut stderr = child.stderr.take();
509:     let stdout_reader = std::thread::spawn(move || drain(&mut stdout));
510:     let stderr_reader = std::thread::spawn(move || drain(&mut stderr));
511:     let status = loop {
512:         match child.try_wait() {
513:             Ok(Some(status)) => break status,
514:             Ok(None) => {}
515:             Err(_) => return None,
516:         }
517:         // F13: a per-request cancel (spawn_radio's timeout Err branch sets it)
518:         // kills the child on the next 50ms poll instead of letting a radio
519:         // chain keep spawning Python for ~40s after the UI has given up.
520:         if cancel.as_ref().is_some_and(|c| c.load(Ordering::Relaxed)) {
521:             liblog(format!("yt: {bin} killed on cancellation"));
522:             let _ = child.kill();
523:             break child.wait().ok()?;
524:         }
525:         if Instant::now() >= deadline {
526:             liblog(format!("yt: {bin} killed after exceeding its deadline"));
527:             let _ = child.kill();
528:             break child.wait().ok()?;
529:         }
530:         std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50));
531:     };
532:     // Both pipes EOF once the process is gone (kill included), so these joins
533:     // cannot hang.
534:     let out = stdout_reader.join().ok()?;
535:     let err = stderr_reader.join().ok()?;
536:     if !status.success() {
537:         let code = status.code().unwrap_or(-1);
538:         let tail = String::from_utf8_lossy(&err)
539:             .lines()
540:             .next_back()
541:             .unwrap_or("")
542:             .to_string();
543:         liblog(format!(
544:             "yt: {bin} exited {code}: {tail} (args {:?})",
545:             extra.iter().take(3).collect::<Vec<_>>()
546:         ));
547:         return None;
548:     }
549:     String::from_utf8(out).ok()
550: }
551: 
552: /// Read one pipe to EOF into a vector. Runs on the reader threads; EOF is
553: /// guaranteed by the process exiting (or being killed).
554: fn drain<R: std::io::Read + Send>(pipe: &mut Option<R>) -> Vec<u8> {
555:     let mut buf = Vec::new();
556:     if let Some(pipe) = pipe.as_mut() {
557:         let _ = pipe.read_to_end(&mut buf);
558:     }
559:     buf
560: }

857:     /// the same child runs into the deadline and is killed there.

859:     #[test]

862:         let bin = path.to_string_lossy().into_owned();

864:         let cancel = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
865:         let cancel_t = cancel.clone();
866:         let bin_t = bin.clone();
867:         let t0 = Instant::now();
868:         let handle =
869:             std::thread::spawn(move || yt_stdout_with_bin(&bin_t, &["-J"], &[], Some(cancel_t)));
870:         std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(200));
871:         cancel.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
872:         assert!(handle.join().expect("worker thread").is_none());
873:         assert!(
874:             t0.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(2),
875:             "cancel must kill the child fast, took {:?}",
876:             t0.elapsed()
877:         );

879:         let t1 = Instant::now();
880:         assert!(yt_stdout_with_bin(&bin, &["-J"], &[], None).is_none());
881:         assert!(
882:             t1.elapsed() >= Duration::from_secs(10),
883:             "an uncancelled child must hit the 15s deadline, returned after {:?}",
884:             t1.elapsed()
885:         );
886:

891:     /// the call site fails open, it never becomes a failure — and acquires
892:     /// instantly when a permit is free. A local semaphore keeps the global
893:     /// `YTDLP_PERMIT` untouched (tests run in parallel).

898:         assert!(
899:             wait_for_permit(&p, Instant::now() - Duration::from_secs(1)).is_none(),
900:             "a passed deadline must give up, not block"

902:         drop(_hold);
903:         assert!(
904:             wait_for_permit(&p, Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(5)).is_some(),
905:             "a free permit must be acquired instantly"
```

```text
3: //! Keyed on artist/title/album/duration rather than a provider track id, so it

6: //! same query. This is the `src/api/lyrics.rs` body, relocated into the library
7: //! so it outlives the bin-side api layer.

17: type MemoValue = (Vec<(u32, String)>, bool);

19: /// One client for the whole process: lrclib fetches are rare (one per track
20: /// change) but each used to build a fresh client — TLS setup + connection
21: /// pool per request. `reqwest::blocking::Client` is `Send + Sync`, so a
22: /// shared instance is sound across the worker threads.
23: static CLIENT: OnceLock<reqwest::blocking::Client> = OnceLock::new();
24: 
25: /// Session-scoped memo of lrclib results, keyed on the exact request URL
26: /// (F12). Repeated tracks — the same song again, radio loops — used to
27: /// re-fetch identical content on every track change; the memo kills the
28: /// duplicate roundtrip. Session scope on purpose: entries die at relaunch,
29: /// so lyrics added upstream since the last run are picked up (no
30: /// never-cache-empty trap, no TTL needed).
31: static MEMO: LazyLock<Mutex<HashMap<String, MemoValue>>> =
32:     LazyLock::new(|| Mutex::new(HashMap::new()));
33: 
34: /// Fetch lyrics for a track from lrclib. Returns `(lines, synced)`; synced
35: /// lines carry timestamps, plain text has none. An empty first half means no
36: /// match — the caller renders the view empty.
37: pub fn fetch_lyrics_blocking(
38:     artist: &str,
39:     title: &str,
40:     album: &str,
41:     duration_ms: u32,
42: ) -> (Vec<(u32, String)>, bool) {
43:     let client = CLIENT.get_or_init(|| crate::httpcache::blocking_client().clone());
44:     let url = format!(
45:         "https://lrclib.net/api/get?artist_name={}&track_name={}&album_name={}&duration={}",
46:         urlencode(artist),
47:         urlencode(title),
48:         urlencode(album),
49:         duration_ms / 1000
50:     );

52: }

56: /// one session. The client is injected so tests can point the miss path at an
57: /// offline endpoint without touching the real lrclib.net. Never holds the
58: /// lock across the network fetch (a memo miss must not serialize fetches).
59: fn fetch_lyrics_memo(client: &reqwest::blocking::Client, url: &str) -> (Vec<(u32, String)>, bool) {

102:     /// The memo must serve a second identical request without touching the
103:     /// network. The first call caches the (empty) miss against a dead port;
104:     /// a server on the same port then serves real lyrics, and the second
105:     /// call — same URL — still returns the CACHED empty value, proving no

109:         // Reserve a port, then close it: the first call's URL is unreachable.
110:         let port = std::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0")
111:             .unwrap()
112:             .local_addr()
113:             .unwrap()
114:             .port();
115:         let url = format!(
116:             "http://127.0.0.1:{port}/api/get?artist_name=a&track_name=b&album_name=c&duration=1"
117:         );
118:         let client = reqwest::blocking::Client::new();
119: 
120:         // Call 1 — connection refused: the miss result is memoized.
121:         assert_eq!(fetch_lyrics_memo(&client, &url), (Vec::new(), false));
122:         assert_eq!(MEMO.lock().unwrap().len(), 1);
123: 
124:         // Serve real lyrics on the very same URL now.
125:         let listener = std::net::TcpListener::bind(("127.0.0.1", port)).unwrap();
126:         std::thread::spawn(move || {
127:             use std::io::{Read, Write};
128:             if let Ok((mut sock, _)) = listener.accept() {
129:                 let mut buf = [0u8; 4096];
130:                 let _ = sock.read(&mut buf);
131:                 let body = r#"{"syncedLyrics":"[00:01.00]hello there","plainLyrics":null}"#;
132:                 let _ = sock.write_all(
133:                     format!(
134:                         "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\nContent-Length: {}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n{}",
135:                         body.len(),
136:                         body
137:                     )
138:                     .as_bytes(),
139:                 );
140:             }
141:         });
142: 
143:         // Call 2 — identical args: the memo returns the cached miss and never
144:         // touches the (now live) server; a real fetch would return lyrics.
145:         assert_eq!(fetch_lyrics_memo(&client, &url), (Vec::new(), false));
146:         assert_eq!(MEMO.lock().unwrap().len(), 1);
147:     }
```
