84: }
85: 
86: /// Write `bytes` to `path` atomically: a uniquely-named temp sibling, fsync,
87: /// then rename over the destination. Returns true when the rename landed; on
88: /// any failure the temp is removed and false is returned — a torn write can
89: /// never become the visible file.
90: ///
91: /// The rename-over-existing fallback covers Windows, where the rename can
92: /// fail over a destination that is open or otherwise locked: the destination
93: /// is removed and the rename retried once. The fallback deletes the old file
94: /// before the second rename, so a failure there leaves `path` absent — the
95: /// state.json caller keeps `.bak` to cover the gap; on unix the first rename
96: /// replaces in place and the fallback is effectively unreachable.
97: ///
98: /// `pub` because the persistence caller lives in the binary crate; only the
99: /// lib crate's own modules could see a `pub(crate)` item.
100: pub fn write_atomic(path: &Path, bytes: &[u8]) -> bool {
101:     let tmp = tmp_sibling(path);
102:     if std::fs::File::create(&tmp)
103:         .and_then(|mut f| {
104:             f.write_all(bytes)?;
105:             f.sync_all()
106:         })
107:         .is_err()
108:     {
109:         let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&tmp);
110:         return false;
111:     }
112:     if std::fs::rename(&tmp, path).is_ok() {
113:         return true;
114:     }
115:     // Windows: rename cannot replace an existing destination — remove first.
116:     // Never run on Unix: a failed first rename fails identically after
117:     // remove, so the destination would be deleted for nothing.
118:     #[cfg(windows)]
119:     {
120:         if std::fs::remove_file(path).is_ok() && std::fs::rename(&tmp, path).is_ok() {
121:             return true;
122:         }
123:     }
124:     let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&tmp);
125:     false
126: }
127: 
128: /// Split any `scheme:kind:id` URI into its three parts. The port's `yt:`
129: /// URIs parse here, as do the synthetic `tuna:action:` rows; consumers that
130: /// care about kind match on it by name, not position.
131: pub fn uri_parts(uri: &str) -> Option<(&str, &str, &str)> {
132:     let mut p = uri.split(':');
133:     match (p.next(), p.next(), p.next()) {
134:         // Lenient by design: matches the pre-port contract (tests/util.rs locks
135:         // in trailing-segment tolerance and empty-id acceptance as quirks).
136:         (Some(scheme), Some(kind), Some(id)) => Some((scheme, kind, id)),
137:         _ => None,
138:     }
139: }
140: 
141: /// Convert a `yt:kind:id` URI to its youtube.com equivalent. Other schemes
142: /// (the synthetic `tuna:action:` rows) have no shareable URL and return "".
143: /// The video/playlist shapes delegate to the single-owner builders below;
144: /// the channel card (`/channel/{id}`) stays distinct from the uploads tab
145: /// ([`channel_videos_url`]) that drill-ins expand.
146: pub fn uri_to_url(uri: &str) -> String {
147:     let Some((scheme, kind, id)) = uri_parts(uri) else {
148:         return String::new();
149:     };
150:     match (scheme, kind) {
151:         ("yt", "video") => video_url(uri).unwrap_or_default(),
152:         ("yt", "playlist") => playlist_uri(id),
153:         ("yt", "channel") => format!("https://www.youtube.com/channel/{id}"),
154:         _ => String::new(),
155:     }
156: }
157: 
158: /// Normalize a video id / `yt:video:` uri / watch URL to a watch URL. These
159: /// builders own the canonical youtube.com shapes, so every layer (the yt
160: /// resolver, the expander, browse) shares one spelling.
161: pub fn video_url(url_or_id: &str) -> Option<String> {
162:     if url_or_id.starts_with("http://") || url_or_id.starts_with("https://") {
163:         return Some(url_or_id.to_string());
164:     }
165:     if let Some(id) = track_id_from_uri(url_or_id) {
166:         return Some(format!("https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={id}"));
167:     }
168:     // A bare id — but only a bare one: a `yt:playlist:` or other non-video uri
169:     // must not masquerade as a video id.
170:     if url_or_id.contains(':') {
171:         return None;
172:     }
173:     (!url_or_id.is_empty()).then(|| format!("https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={url_or_id}"))
174: }
175: 
176: /// The canonical playlist URL.
177: pub fn playlist_uri(id: &str) -> String {
178:     format!("https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list={id}")
179: }
180: 
181: /// The canonical channel uploads tab — what a `yt:channel:` drill-in expands.
182: pub fn channel_videos_url(id: &str) -> String {
183:     format!("https://www.youtube.com/channel/{id}/videos")
184: }
185: 
186: /// Pull the id out of a `yt:video:<id>` URI.
187: pub fn track_id_from_uri(uri: &str) -> Option<String> {
188:     match uri_parts(uri) {
189:         Some(("yt", "video", id)) => Some(id.to_string()),
190:         _ => None,
191:     }
192: }
193: 
194: /// Percent-encode a string for use in a query component.
195: pub fn urlencode(s: &str) -> String {
196:     let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len());
197:     for b in s.bytes() {
198:         match b {
199:             b'A'..=b'Z' | b'a'..=b'z' | b'0'..=b'9' | b'-' | b'_' | b'.' | b'~' => {
200:                 out.push(b as char)
201:             }
202:             _ => out.push_str(&format!("%{b:02X}")),
203:         }
204:     }
205:     out
206: }

3: /// Parse LRC `[mm:ss.xx] text` lines into sorted (ms, text) pairs.
4: pub fn parse_lrc(lrc: &str) -> Vec<(u32, String)> {
5:     let mut out: Vec<(u32, String)> = Vec::new();
6:     for line in lrc.lines() {
7:         // A line may carry multiple timestamps; collect them, then the trailing text.
8:         let mut rest = line;
9:         let mut stamps: Vec<u32> = Vec::new();
10:         while rest.starts_with('[') {
11:             let Some(end) = rest.find(']') else { break };
12:             let tag = &rest[1..end];
13:             if let Some(ms) = parse_lrc_stamp(tag) {

16:             // Keep consuming bracket groups even if this one was not a

21:             rest = rest[end + 1..].trim_start();
22:         }
23:         let text = rest.trim().to_string();
24:         for ms in stamps {
25:             out.push((ms, text.clone()));
26:         }
27:     }

29:     out
30: }

33: pub fn parse_lrc_stamp(tag: &str) -> Option<u32> {
34:     // mm:ss.xx or mm:ss
35:     let (mm, rest) = tag.split_once(':')?;
36:     let mm: u32 = mm.parse().ok()?;

/// Legacy wrapper kept for tests that call fetch_lyrics_memo directly.
/// Now keyed on memo_key + duration, with 0-duration guard.
fn fetch_lyrics_memo(client: &reqwest::blocking::Client, url: &str) -> (Vec<(u32, String)>, bool) {
    // Back-compat: extract expected duration from url if present, else 0.
    // This keeps the old test harness (which constructs raw URLs) working.
    let expected = url
        .split("duration=")
        .nth(1)
        .and_then(|s| s.split('&').next())
        .and_then(|d| d.parse::<f64>().ok())
        .unwrap_or(0.0);
    fetch_lyrics_memo_with_expected(client, url, expected)
}

fn fetch_lyrics_memo_with_expected(
    client: &reqwest::blocking::Client,
    url: &str,
    expected_s: f64,
) -> (Vec<(u32, String)>, bool) {
    // Derive memo key from url+expected — preserves F1 fix for direct callers
    let memo_key = format!("{}|{}", url, expected_s as u32);
    // 0-duration guard: don't memoize
    if expected_s == 0.0 {
        return fetch_lyrics_url(client, url, expected_s);
    }
    if let Some(hit) = MEMO.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner()).get(&memo_key) {
        return hit.clone();
    }
    let result = fetch_lyrics_url(client, url, expected_s);
    MEMO.lock()
        .unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner())
        .insert(memo_key, result.clone());
    result
}

/// One lrclib GET + parse — the network core, split out of the memo wrapper
/// so the cache path is testable without real network (F12). `synced` lines
/// carry timestamps, plain text has none; an empty first half means no match.
///
/// `/api/search` (the production URL) answers with an array: `pick_search_match`
/// narrows it by duration before the lyrics are read. A single-record response
/// (the old `/api/get` shape) is used as-is.
fn fetch_lyrics_url(client: &reqwest::blocking::Client, url: &str, expected_duration_s: f64) -> (Vec<(u32, String)>, bool) {
    let Ok(resp) = client
        .get(url)
        .header("User-Agent", "tuna-tui (terminal music player)")
        .send()
    else {
        return (Vec::new(), false);
    };
    if !resp.status().is_success() {
        return (Vec::new(), false);
    }
    let Ok(v) = resp.json::<serde_json::Value>() else {
        return (Vec::new(), false);
    };
    // Filtered search path vs single record: use tolerance-aware picking
    if v.is_array() {
        // Use primary tolerance here; fallback chain widens via fetch_with_fallback
        // but direct callers (tests) expect the string tolerance behavior.
        // To preserve both, try primary then fallback.
        if let Some(record) = pick_search_match(&v, expected_duration_s, PRIMARY_TOLERANCE_S)
            .or_else(|| pick_search_match(&v, expected_duration_s, FALLBACK_TOLERANCE_S))
        {
            return lyrics_from_record(record);
        }
        return (Vec::new(), false);
    }
    // Single-record: must have lyrics
    if !has_lyrics(&v) {
        return (Vec::new(), false);
    }
    lyrics_from_record(&v)
}

/// Read `syncedLyrics` (preferred) or `plainLyrics` off one lrclib record.
fn lyrics_from_record(record: &serde_json::Value) -> (Vec<(u32, String)>, bool) {
    if let Some(synced) = record["syncedLyrics"].as_str().filter(|s| !s.is_empty()) {
        return (crate::lyrics::parse::parse_lrc(synced), true);
    }
    if let Some(plain) = record["plainLyrics"].as_str().filter(|s| !s.is_empty()) {
        let lines = plain.lines().map(|l| (0u32, l.to_string())).collect();
        return (lines, false);
    }
    (Vec::new(), false)
}
